entries.title: Wildcard Support for Network Segments
body: You can define Network segments in VPN (for Legacy Apps) using wildcard entries (e.g., *.domain.com). This streamlines configuration for environments with FQDNs.
This feature is only supported on Zscaler Client Connector version 5.0 and later for Windows.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring Network Segments.

entries.title: Enhancements for End User Isolation Experience
body: Enhancements have been made to several features of the end user isolation experience. Depending on your isolation profile settings, you can explore the following features and functionalities in the Zero Trust Mode menu during an isolated session:
- Clipboard: Use clipboard functions (e.g., copy and paste) and view notifications about clipboard restrictions. To learn more, see Using Clipboard in Isolation.
- Translate: Translate the entire web page or selected text from the web page into your preferred language. To learn more, see Understanding Language Translate for Isolation.
- Find: Search text within the web page.
- Troubleshoot: View network latency and export isolation session logs. To learn more, see Accessing Network Latency in Isolation.
See image.
To learn more, see Using the Zero Trust Mode Menu in Native Browser Experience.

entries.title: Support for Nested Criteria, NOT Operators, and Bulk Actions in Global Rules and Policy Groups
body: Private Access (ZPA) added the following updates for global rules and policy groups to simplify the management of application access policies:
- Added support for building nested criteria sets when configuring rules with SAML or SCIM Attributes or Client Connector Posture Profiles.
- Added support for applying AND NOT and OR NOT logic operators when configuring rules with SAML or SCIM Attributes or Client Connector Posture Profiles.
- Added support for bulk move and delete rules within policy groups.
To learn more, see:

entries.title: Enterprise Browser for Mobile
body: Enterprise Browser for Zero Trust Browser is available as a native mobile application for iOS, iPadOS, and Android. On a personal or corporate phone or tablet, the Enterprise Browser mobile app provides a governed workspace that enforces policy, prevents data loss, and protects users from everyday browser-based threats.
See image.

Distribution of the app depends on whether the device is personal, corporate managed, or enrolled in a bring-your-own-device (BYOD) program. Users can install the app from the App Store or Google Play, or admins can push the app to users via your organization's Mobile Device Management (MDM) or Mobile Application Management (MAM) platform.
To learn more, see Understanding Enterprise Browser for Mobile.

entries.title: Adaptive Traffic Steering
body: Adaptive Traffic Steering automatically redirects application traffic to healthier network paths when network degradation affects connectivity or performance. This helps maintain application availability and minimize service disruptions caused by network congestion, packet loss, increased latency, and regional network outages.

You can enable Adaptive Traffic Steering for application segments in organizations that have Business Continuity configured. When enabled, Private Access (ZPA) uses real-time network health metrics to identify degraded paths and redirect traffic to alternative paths.
For more information, see Understanding Adaptive Traffic Steering⁠.

entries.title: Global Rules and Policy Groups for Application Access
body: Private Access (ZPA) supports global rules and policy groups to simplify the management of application access policies.
Global rules let you define common rule logic once and apply it consistently across application access policies, reducing repetitive configuration and helping maintain consistent policy enforcement.
See image.
To learn more, see About Access Policies for Global Rules.

Policy groups provide a logical way to organize related application access policies by grouping rules that share common access requirements. Common criteria configured at the policy group level are automatically applied to every rule in the group and combined with each rule's criteria. This simplifies policy management, reduces repetitive configuration, and improves scalability as your deployment grows.
See image.
To learn more, see About Access Policies for Policy Groups.

entries.title: ZPA API Support for Policy Groups
body: The Private Access (ZPA) API includes the following endpoints to extend programmatic access to various Private Access features and functionalities:
- Policy Groups
- GET /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/policyGroupSet/{groupSetId}/group/all
- GET /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/policyGroupSet/{groupSetId}/group/{groupId}
- DELETE /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/policyGroupSet/{groupSetId}/group/{groupId}
- POST /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/policyGroupSet/{groupSetId}/group/search
- POST /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/policyGroupSet/{groupSetId}/group
- PUT /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/policyGroupSet/{groupSetId}/group/{groupId}
- PUT /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/policyGroupSet/{groupSetId}/group/{groupId}/reorder/{newOrder}
- Policy Group Rules
- GET /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/policyGroupSet/{groupSetId}/group/{groupId}/rule
- GET /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/policyGroupSet/{groupSetId}/group/{groupId}/rule/{ruleId}
- DELETE /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/policyGroupSet/{groupSetId}/group/{groupId}/rule/{ruleId}
- POST /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/policyGroupSet/{groupSetId}/group/{groupId}/rule
- PUT /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/policyGroupSet/{groupSetId}/group/{groupId}/rule/{ruleId}/reorder/{newOrder}
- Policy Group Sets
- GET /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/policyGroupSet
- GET /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/policyGroupSet/{groupSetId}
- GET /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/policyGroupSet/policyType/{policyType}
- GET /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/policyGroupSet/policyType/{policyType}/summary
- GET /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/policyGroupSet/policyType/{policyType}/summaryStats

After global rules and policy groups are enabled, the legacy access policy ZPA API calls are not supported for managing policies. If you manage access policies through the legacy ZPA API or Infrastructure as Code (IaC), you must update your ZPA API automation and IaC workflows to use the new API before enabling this feature.
To learn more, see:
- Global Rules and Policy Groups for Application Access
- Configuring Policy Groups Using API
- Configuring Policy Group Rules Using API
- Obtaining Policy Group Set Details Using API

entries.title: Notification Service Updates for VPN (for Legacy Apps)
body: The Notifications service supports Network Connector and VPN Service Edge notifications for the VPN (for Legacy Apps) category for the following Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) events:
- Established peers count dropped: Indicates when the total number of active, established BGP sessions falls below a specified threshold.
- Network routes count dropped: Indicates when there is a significant decrease in the number of network routes (prefixes) being received.
- Peer disconnected: Indicates when a specific BGP session with a peer transitions to disconnected.
- Peer extended downtime: Indicates when a BGP peer remains disconnected for a prolonged period.
- Peer flapping: Indicates when a BGP peer's session repeatedly and rapidly cycles between up and down.
VPN Service Edge also supports notifications for the System Resource category for a CPU starvation event.
To learn more, see Support for VPN (for Legacy Apps) Notifications.

entries.title: Support for IdP Attribute-Based VPN Access Policy

To learn more, see About IP Address Objects and About IdP Attribute Objects.

entries.title: Actions for Upgrading Agent Groups in Microsegmentation
body: You can take the following actions when upgrading virtual machine (VM) agent groups for Microsegmentation in the Zscaler Admin Console:
- Halt an upgrade that is in progress from the Upgrade Status column on the Agent Groups page.
- See image.

- Set the upgrade window when configuring an agent group. For example, if you start the upgrade at 8:00 AM and set the upgrade window to 12 hours, then the final agent upgrade required for the group starts no later than 8:00 PM.
- See image.
- Select the upgrade sequence (Serial or Parallel) and strategy (Halt next agent upgrade or Skip to next agent) when initiating an on-demand upgrade.
- See image.
To learn more, see About Agent Groups, Configuring Agent Groups, and Managing Agent Groups.

entries.title: Flow Log Aggregations for Microsegmentation
body: The Flow Log Aggregations page for Microsegmentation in the Zscaler Admin Console provides insight into your organization's aggregated network flows. You can view flows within a specific time period (up to the last 14 days) and filter the flows by AppZone and further by the source and destination resource groups within that AppZone.
See image.
To learn more, see About Flow Log Aggregations.

entries.title: Perimeter Policies for Resource Groups in Microsegmentation
body: Perimeter policies allow you to systematically secure managed resource groups in Microsegmentation. You can create perimeter policies to easily define how Microsegmentation handles the resource group's inbound, outbound, and internal traffic (e.g., Block, Sim Block, Allow).
You can create a perimeter policy from the new Perimeter Policies page in the Zscaler Admin Console or from the Resource Groups page when creating a resource group.
See image.
To learn more, see About Perimeter Policies, Adding a Perimeter Policy, and Configuring Resource Groups.

entries.title: Policy Recommendations for Resource Groups in Microsegmentation
body: Microsegmentation provides policy recommendations for resource groups based on historical network flows. When selecting a resource group on the Application Map in the Zscaler Admin Console, you can view managed and unmanaged flows in a table. At the same time, a drawer opens with the option to review policy recommendations based on these flows.
See image.

Recommendations are listed on a page within the resource group. You can filter managed and unmanaged flows by direction (i.e., inbound and outbound). You can review and accept a recommendation as is, quickly applying the new policy and protecting flows. Alternatively, you can edit the recommendation, resolving conflicts as required, before applying it as a new policy or merging it with an existing policy for your organization.
See image.
To learn more, see Viewing the Application Map, About Policy Recommendations for Resource Groups, and Reviewing Policy Recommendations for Resource Groups.

entries.title: Emergency Access Integration with Authentication Service
body: Emergency access for Privileged Remote Access (PRA) is supported for tenants subscribed to Authentication Service for users. As part of this change, the IdP API Token field is hidden, and the User Group Name field is disabled on the Emergency Access page.

Authentication Service must be used as an identity provider (IdP) instead of Okta after migrating Private Access (ZPA) tenants to Authentication Service. Additionally, tenants subscribed to Authentication Service must add a guest domain with Arbitrary Guest Domains enabled, and must ensure that the guest user is assigned to the Zscaler Emergency Access User Group in Authentication Service.
To learn more, see:
- Configuring Emergency Access
- Adding Guest Domains

- Assigning Entitlements to Users and Groups

entries.title: Enhancements for End User Isolation Experience for Clipboard Functions

entries.title: Enhancements for End User Isolation Experience for File Transfers
body: The following updates have been made to the end user isolation experience for Zero Trust Browser:

- Download Completion: When a user downloads a file while in isolation, a temporary notification appears to confirm when the file has completed downloading. The user can click the View button from the notification to see the file name and location in the Protected Storage. Additionally, they can click the Protected Storage icon from the Zero Trust Mode menu to open the Protected Storage section and view all file transfer notifications.
- See image.

- Upload Options: A user can upload a file in multiple different ways while in isolation, such as using the Upload File button in the Protected Storage and uploading files from their local machine to a website.
- See image.
To learn more, see Using the Zero Trust Mode Menu in Native Browser Experience and Transferring and Viewing Files in Isolation.

entries.title: Enhancements for End User Isolation Experience Session Indicator & Menu
body: The Zero Trust Mode icon that indicates a live isolation session for Zero Trust Browser hides an expandable menu for the user to access different functions:
- The Protected Storage icon allows users to view all file transfers for the isolation session.
- The Clipboard icon allows users to view notifications about clipboard functions and restrictions.
- The Print icon allows users to view options and information for printing settings.
- The Troubleshoot icon allows users to start a debug session, view network latency, access ip.zscaler.com, or export isolation session logs.
- The Information icon allows users to view the settings configured by admins for an isolation profile. This includes user restrictions and disabled tools.
Clicking the checkmark Zero Trust Mode icon at the bottom of the menu collapses the options back under the floating icon.
See image.
To learn more, see Using the Zero Trust Mode Menu in Native Browser Experience.

You can create Partner Federation requests, manage incoming and outgoing requests, and manage federated partners that have established trust. entries.title: Automatic Session Restore for Isolation

This feature is different from Persistent State, which is enabled per isolation profile to carry over data from an expired session to a new session.

entries.title: OAuth 2.0 Enrollment Support for Private Cloud Controllers
body: An update was released to support OAuth 2.0 enrollment for Private Cloud Controllers. OAuth 2.0 is the recommended method for enrollment for Private Access (ZPA), but provisioning key enrollment is also supported. To use OAuth 2.0, the OAuth server FQDN zpa-oauth.private.zscaler.com must be allowlisted, and user devices must be allowed to make an outbound connection to the zpa-oauth.private.zscaler.com server. Refer to config.zscaler.com/private.zscaler.com/zpa (for the private.zscaler.com cloud) or config.zscaler.com/zpatwo.net/zpa (for the zpatwo.net cloud) for the IP address to add to the allowlist.
OAuth 2.0 support is available with a minimum version of Manager software and Private Cloud Controller version 25.47.3.

Supported virtual machine (VM) images automatically have this feature enabled. Provisioning key enrollment is also supported on all VM images. The image attempts to use OAuth enrollment tokens by default but applies a provisioning key first if one is available.
The OAuth server only supports IPv4-based communication. If a Private Cloud Controller only has an IPV6 address, it cannot access the OAuth server.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring Private Cloud Controllers.

Refer to config.zscaler.com/private.zscaler.com/zpa (for the private.zscaler.com cloud) or config.zscaler.com/zpatwo.net/zpa (for the zpatwo.net cloud) for the IP address to add to the allowlist.
OAuth 2.0 support is available with a minimum version of Manager software and Private Service Edge version 25.48.4.

Supported virtual machine (VM) images automatically have this feature enabled with the exception of Docker. Provisioning key enrollment is also supported on all VM images. The image attempts to use OAuth enrollment tokens by default but applies a provisioning key first if one is available.
The OAuth server only supports IPv4-based communication. If a Private Service Edge only has an IPV6 address, it cannot access the OAuth server.

entries.title: Updates to Private Access (ZPA)
body: The Private Access (ZPA) API includes the following endpoints to extend programmatic access to various ZPA features and functionalities:
- App Connector Group Management
- GET /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/appConnectorGroup
- Browser Access Groups Management
- GET /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/browserAccessGroups
- Business Continuity Settings
- GET /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/businessContinuitySettings
- PUT /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/BusinessContinuitySettings/{id}
- GET /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/BusinessContinuitySettings/metadata
- GET /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/BusinessContinuitySettings/certificate
- Enrollment Certificates
- GET /mgmtconfig/v2/admin/customers/{customerId}/enrollmentCert
- Log Streaming (LSS) Configuration
- GET /mgmtconfig/v2/admin/customers/{customerId}/lssConfig
- Private Cloud Management
- GET /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/privateCloud
- POST /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/privateCloud
- GET /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/privateCloud/{privateCloudId}
- PUT /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/privateCloud/{privateCloudId}
- DELETE /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/privateCloud/{privateCloudId}
- Provisioning Key Management
- GET /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/associationType/{associationType}/provisioningKey
- DELETE /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/associationType/{associationType}/provisioningKey/{provisioningKeyId}
- GET /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/associationType/{associationType}/provisioningKey/{provisioningKeyId}
- PUT /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/associationType/{associationType}/provisioningKey/{provisioningKeyId}
- Service Edge Group Management
- GET /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/serviceEdgeGroup
- Version Profiles
- GET /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/visible/versionProfiles
- GET /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/versionProfile
The ZPA API is accessible via OneAPI and via legacy API endpoints. The following endpoints extend programmatic access to various ZPA features and functionalities:
- Private Cloud Controller Management
- GET /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/privateCloud

entries.title: Support for End User Migration to Authentication Service
body: An update was released to provide support for end user migration to Authentication Service. This update ensures that the set of existing Private Access (ZPA) end users and their entitlements remain accurate and consistent throughout the migration process. During migration, external IdP configurations are view only. After migration is complete, the following conditions apply:
- IdP configurations are inactive but can be restored if necessary.
- Private Access no longer syncs users from external IdPs, and new external IdP configurations are not allowed.
- Authentication Service becomes the identity service for all Zscaler products, centralizing all identity management.
As part of this release, you can select the External IAM IdP (i.e., the external IdP attribute created in Authentication Service) when configuring a policy or a Microtenant.

To learn more, see Migrating Private Access End Users to Authentication Service, Migrating End Users to Authentication Service, Migrating Zscaler Service Admins to Authentication Service, Configuring Microtenants, Policies, and Support for End User Migration.

entries.title: Agent Telemetry Status Changes
body: Several new statuses are available for filtering Agent Telemetry results.
For agents, the following statuses are available:
- Up to Date: The new agent upgrade version number is either greater than or equal to the agent version number of its corresponding agent group.
- Pending: The new agent upgrade version number is less than the agent version number of its corresponding agent group.
- In Progress: The agent is actively upgrading, and will complete within 10 minutes of reaching this status.
- Forced Upgrade: The agent has manually been upgraded by an admin outside its configured upgrade schedule.
- Failed: An upgrade attempt has failed.
- N/A: The agent or its agent group is disabled.
For agent groups, the following statuses are available:
- Up to Date: All agents are up-to-date.
- Pending: At least one agent in the agent group is in a pending status for the latest agent version.
- In Progress: At least one agent in the agent group is actively upgrading.
- In Progress with Failures: Multiple agents in an agent group are upgrading with some in a failed state and the remaining agents proceeding.
- Failed: All agents within an agent group have reached a failed state.
- Completed with Failures: All agents within an agent group have completed the upgrade process with some in a failed state.
- N/A: The agent group is disabled.
To learn more, see About Agent Telemetry.

entries.title: Tag Management for Defined Application Segments
body: Private Access (ZPA) supports Tag Management, which enables you to create, organize, and manage tags for classifying and grouping resources more effectively. Tag Management standardizes tagging across environments to simplify policy configuration and improve visibility into related resources within Private Access. To learn more, see About Tag Management for Application Segments.
See image.

With Tag Management, you can configure namespaces to logically organize tags and avoid naming conflicts, as well as add and configure tags within those namespaces. When configuring namespaces, you can assign optional values to tags to enable discovery and logical grouping, and configure tag groups by grouping related tags using shared values. To learn more, see Configuring Tags and Namespaces for Application Segments.
See image.
Namespaces and tags can be assigned to defined application segments. To learn more, see Configuring Defined Application Segments.
See image.
Tag groups and tag values can be assigned to access policies. To learn more, see Configuring Access Policy.
See image.
The maximum number of tags that can be created per Microtenant is 25,000. The maximum number of tags that can be created per customer is 25,000. To learn more, see Ranges & Limitations.

Customers with the Segmentation add-on license can request to update the total number of recommendations from 100 to 500.

You can view the analytics of Client Connector Trusted Networks by selecting the Timeout Policy Blocks on the User Activity Diagnostics page.

entries.title: Replacing or Migrating Existing Network Connectors with Network Connectors that Support Redundancy
body: For customers who are not yet running Network Connectors that support redundancy, Zscaler strongly recommends replacing or migrating existing Network Connectors with redundancy-capable Network Connectors. Network Connectors that support redundancy resolve the following failure scenarios:
- A Network Connector link failure
- An internal link failure towards customer routers
- An external link failure towards the VPN Service Edge
- A complete Network Connector node failure
- A data center failure with traffic rerouting towards another data center
- Scaling - ECMP (equal-cost multi-path) load balancing across Network Connectors from the VPN Service Edges and customer routers towards the Network Connector
The redundancy design is based on External Border Gateway Protocol (EBGP) routing.
To learn more, see High Availability and Redundancy in VPN (for Legacy Apps) and Replacing or Migrating Existing Network Connectors with Network Connectors that Support Redundancy.

entries.title: Credential Management for Privileged Remote Access
body: You can deploy a credential agent to automate the discovery, synchronization, and lifecycle management of privileged credentials for Privileged Remote Access (PRA) in the Zscaler Admin Console. After configuring the credential agent, you can:
- Automatically discover credentials using LDAP queries from Active Directory (AD) or search queries from Microsoft Entra AD.
- Rotate credentials to generate new passwords with defined security requirements.
- Create rotation policies to set rotation schedules for credentials.
- Apply filters to automatically identify and pull newly created credentials from the AD.

entries.title: OAuth 2.0 Enrollment Support for App Connectors
body: An update was released to support OAuth 2.0 enrollment for App Connectors. OAuth 2.0 is the recommended method for enrollment for ZPA, but provisioning key enrollment is also supported. To use OAuth 2.0, the OAuth server FQDN zpa-oauth.private.zscaler.com must be allowlisted, and user devices must be allowed to make an outbound connection to the zpa-oauth.private.zscaler.com server. Refer to config.zscaler.com/private.zscaler.com/zpa (for the private.zscaler.com cloud) or config.zscaler.com/zpatwo.net/zpa (for the zpatwo.net cloud) for the IP address to add to the allowlist.
OAuth 2.0 support is available with a Manager software and App Connector version 25.48.4.

Supported virtual machine (VM) images automatically have this feature enabled with the exception of Kubernetes, OpenShift, and Docker. Provisioning key enrollment is also supported on all VM images. The image attempts to use OAuth enrollment tokens by default but applies a provisioning key first if one is available.
The OAuth server only supports IPv4-based communication. If an App Connector only has an IPV6 address, it cannot access the OAuth server.
OAuth 2.0 enrollment includes the following features:

- The pages for adding App Connectors have been simplified so you only need to select an App Connector group and up to 20 OAuth 2.0 enrollment tokens. If you add an App Connector to a previously created App Connector group without a signing certificate, you can select a certificate and add enrollment tokens from this page. To learn more, see Configuring App Connectors.
- See image.
- The App Connector Groups table contains a new column that shows the number of App Connectors associated with each App Connector group. To learn more, see About App Connector Groups.
- See image.
- The App Connector Groups details page includes a tab that shows the App Connectors in the current group. To learn more, see About App Connector Groups.
- See image.
- You can create App Connector groups before configuring App Connectors to help streamline the process. The following tabs are also available:

- Details tab: Configure group settings, including an option to select a signing certificate. With the previous provisioning key enrollment, the signing certificate was associated with the provisioning key. With this release, the signing certificate is associated with an App Connector group.

- If you have an App Connector group that has its signing certificate associated with a provisioning key, and you add a new App Connector to that group using OAuth 2.0, you must edit the group and add the signing certificate to it.
- Update Settings tab: Set a version profile, select how often updates occur, or pause updates for App Connectors in this group.
- These options are also available when editing App Connector groups.
- See image.

- On the App Connector Provisioning Keys page, you can select a provisioning key name to view details for the key, edit the key, or edit properties for the enrollment certificate. To learn more, see About App Connector Provisioning Keys.
- See image.
- The Add App Connector Provisioning Key page lets you create a provisioning key and associate a group and signing certificate with the key.

entries.title: Access Policies for VPN (for Legacy Apps)
body: VPN (for Legacy Apps) provides access policy rules that can allow or block network traffic on VPN Service Edges. To create a rule, you need to define the source and destination IP addresses as well as the protocol used. An address book consists of Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDRs) and IP addresses that can be used as a source or destination network in multiple policy rules to help organize the network resources to protect.

Per ZPA policy evaluation, VPN (for Legacy Apps) evaluates access policy rules using a top-down, specific-match principle. Traffic that doesn't match any access policy rule is blocked by default. If you are new to VPN (for Legacy Apps), you must create a policy rule to allow any traffic through the VPN tunnel.
VPN (for Legacy Apps) supports a maximum of 1,000 policy rules and 128 address book entries.
This release includes the following enhancements for access policies:
- You can view configured rules and their actions on the Rules page. You can also:
- Search or filter rules.
- Add, edit, or delete rules.
- View how many additional source or destination networks are available. By default, two networks display but if there are more, the number of additional networks appears (e.g., +1).
- Select a value in the Rule Order column to change the order in which rules are evaluated. Rules are evaluated using a top-down, first-match principle.
- Select a rule name to view details for the rule.
- See image.

- When adding a rule for the source or destination network, you can manually enter it, import individual LAN/Client Subnet entries, or select entries from the address book. You can expand the list of added entries under the IP Address field.

- If you manually enter or import LAN/Client Subnet entries, each time you update a Network segment, you must make a corresponding change to the access policy to add the LAN/Client Subnet entries. If you use the address book, any host or subnet added to the address book is automatically added to the access policy.
- See image.
- On the Address Book page, you can view, search, add, edit, or delete defined sets of IP addresses and CIDRs.
- See image.

- You can add a set of IP addresses or CIDRs to the address book. A set of addresses in the address book cannot be nested inside of other address books, but you can reuse IP addresses and CIDRs in different address books.
- See image.

entries.title: ZPA Private Service Edge Version 25.48.4
body: An update was released for ZPA Private Service Edge that includes bug fixes, optimizations, and version enhancements.

Your ZPA Private Service Edge will be updated based on your software update schedule as configured per ZPA Private Service Edge group. To learn more, see Understanding ZPA Private Service Edge Software Upgrades.
To learn more, see Manager Software Updates.

entries.title: Resolved Issues
body: Multiple fixes for agent version zms-1.6.3 have been released to address several issues. Zscaler recommends upgrading to this agent version to avoid any disruption to traffic due to these issues:
- An issue was fixed in the agent where customers would continue to see flow logs from agents after they were disabled by an admin.

- An issue was fixed in the agent where it would fail to reconnect if it detected any network configuration changes after a host reboot. This might continue to occur in cases where a host is configured with one or more virtual interfaces (i.e., in Microsoft clusters, Ubuntu hosts, etc.).
- Agent stability issues were fixed, such as inaccurate service status and configured exceptions that required additional admin management.
- An issue was fixed where an agent, when installed on a supported OS and on a bare metal server, was reported as an Unknown type, failing to be recognized as a valid resource for the applied policy.
- An issue was fixed where the agent policy enforcement engine dropped outbound packets if interleaved between outbound and inbound packet flows.
- An issue was fixed where the agent policy enforcement engine was leaking memory after rule validation against certain flows.

entries.title: Manager Software Updates
body: A recommended update was released that includes updated App Connector and ZPA Private Service Edge RPM packages for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8.x and 9.x, and Private Cloud Controller and Network Connector RPM packages for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.x.
You can download the Manager software for App Connectors, ZPA Private Service Edges, Private Cloud Controllers, or Network Connectors from our repository. The Manager software version is 25.48.4.
To learn more, see Understanding the Manager Software.

entries.title: Filtered Reports for Application and User Group Relationships
body: You can download reports for filtered application segments on the Application and User Group Relationships insights page.
See image.
To learn more, see Viewing Application and User Group Relationships.

entries.title: GCP Prebuilt Image Support for Network Connector
body: A new Network Connector image is available for Google Cloud Platform (GCP) that includes support for upcoming VPN redundancy features.
If you want to enable firewalld on a system running the Network Connector, you must perform additional steps to modify the firewall filter rule for VPN redundancy to work properly.
To learn more, see Network Connector Deployment Prerequisites and Network Connector Software by Platform.

entries.title: High Availability and Redundancy in VPN (for Legacy Apps)
body: VPN (for Legacy Apps) uses Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) to ensure high availability and fault tolerance by providing alternate paths to reach applications during Network Connector node failures and Network Connector to VPN Service Edge path or link failures. If a failure occurs on a Network Connector within a Network Connector group, VPN Service Edges use BGP to reroute traffic to another Network Connector for the specific IP Address subnet or FQDN.
VPN redundancy and the Admin Probe are supported on VPN Service Edges and Network Connectors starting from version 25.46.2 or later.
This release includes the following enhancements for high availability and redundancy:

- Support is available for configuring a global BGP for VPN Service Edges and Network Connectors, including options to use BGP Timers or bidirectional forwarding detection (BFD) to detect session failures. You can also override the global BGP setting when adding or editing individual VPN Service Edges and Network Connectors.
- See image.
- Options for adding an external router to the Network Connector for BGP configuration are available.
- See image.

- An option to advertise LAN segments locally was added for Network Connector groups. When disabled, you can select which routers to use for the Network Connector and set options such as Multi-hop to peer with routers that are multiple network hops away.
- See image.
- Support for selecting multiple Network Connector groups in Network segments is available. To learn more, see Configuring Network Segments and Editing Network Segments.
- See image.
- A new BGP Peers page allows you to view the routing of Network Connectors for each VPN Service Edge to help troubleshoot, and it also shows peers and connection information.
- See image.

- A new Network Connector Throughput chart on the Network Connectors Dashboard lets you monitor throughput to determine when more Network Connectors are needed. To learn more, see Viewing the Network Connectors Dashboard.
- See image.

- A new Redundant Mode option is available to help determine if redundancy is enabled during troubleshooting. You can view this option when expanding a group on the Network Connector Groups page, or by adding the column on the VPN Service Edges page.
- See image.
- You can execute commands with VPN sessions for VPN Service Edges, Network Connectors, and Network Connector groups on the VPN Support Information page.
- See image.
- Outbound VPN tunnels can establish a gateway to VPN Service Edges using a port range from 51820 to 53000. To learn more, see Network Connector Deployment Guide for Linux.

entries.title: Agent Connection Status Log Updates for Microsegmentation
body: The Agent Connection Status Logs have been updated to specify the different reasons why an agent failed to deploy or upgrade.
To learn more, see About Agent Connection Status Logs.

entries.title: Agent Groups for Resource Group Environment in Microsegmentation
body: When configuring resource groups, you can add an Agent Group as an option for Dynamic Criteria. This is listed under a new category named ZMS.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring Resource Groups.

entries.title: Custom Timestamp Tool for Analytics in Microsegmentation
body: A customizable timestamp selector tool has been added for the Analytics Logs tables in Microsegmentation. This is available for Flow Logs, Agent Telemetry, Agent Connection Status Logs, and Event Logs.
See image.
To learn more, see About Flow Logs, About Agent Connection Status Logs, About Agent Telemetry, and About Event Logs.

entries.title: Initial Target Version in Microsegmentation
body: You can specify the initial target version of the agent for an agent group. This means that whenever you start the agent, it automatically checks to see if it needs to update itself to the target version you specify, and apply the update if needed.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring Agent Groups.

entries.title: Manual Agent Upgrade Option for Microsegmentation
body: You can manually upgrade your agents either individually or by initiating an Agent Group upgrade. You can find the Upgrade Now button in the Actions column of the Agents page or Agent Groups page.
See image.
To learn more, see About Agents.

entries.title: API Discovery for AppProtection
body: API Discovery Insights provides you with deeper insight into API logs and API users for AppProtection. The analytics for API Discovery Insights can be viewed on the AppProtection Diagnostics page using the API Insight filter. API Discovery is supported on the Manager software version 25.44.6.

entries.title: Backup Support for Private Cloud Controllers
body: Users can schedule a maximum of 100 backup copies of the configuration and policy downloaded by Private Cloud Controllers to improve reliability and availability. You can restore a backup using a script.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring Business Continuity Settings.

entries.title: Business Continuity Updates
body: Business Continuity includes the following updates:
- A manual override is available to force Private Cloud Controllers, Private Service Edges, and App Connectors into Business Continuity mode. This option is available when editing a Private Cloud.
- See image.
- To learn more, see Editing Private Clouds.

- The Private Clouds page includes a new column that indicates whether Force Business Continuity Mode is enabled. You can also expand the row to view the reconnect interval and the date and time that Force Business Continuity started.
- See image.
- To learn more, see About Private Clouds.
- Existing IdP configurations can be used to authenticate users during Business Continuity.
- See image.
- To learn more, see Configuring Business Continuity Settings.
- The Primary Channel Control Path was moved from the Business Continuity Settings page to the Private Cloud page. To learn more, see Configuring Private Clouds.

- Last sync times are available for Private Cloud Controllers on the Private Cloud Controllers page. The Policy and Configuration Sync indicates the last time the policy and configuration database was synchronized with the Private Cloud Controller.
- See image.
- To learn more, see About Private Cloud Controllers.

- You can create a Private Service Edge group specifically for Business Continuity or Disaster Recovery. When enabled, Private Service Edges in this group are not used for user redirection except when Business Continuity or Disaster Recovery is in effect, or when a redirection policy is configured with the Private Service Edge group.
- See image.
- To learn more, see Configuring Private Service Edges.

entries.title: Private Cloud Controller Support for Remote Troubleshooting
body: You can create sessions for Private Cloud Controllers for remote troubleshooting on the Support Information page of the ZPA Admin Portal.
See image.
To learn more, see Accessing and Viewing Support Information.

entries.title: Support for Private Cloud Controllers in the Notifications Service
body: The Notifications service supports Private Cloud Controllers when configuring a notification. The following events are supported for Private Cloud Controllers:
- Control Connection Disconnected
- CPU Starvation
- Enrollment Completed
- Invalid System Listen IP Configuration
- Last Component Disconnected
- Outdated Component Manager Version
- Provisioning Key Utilization Exceeded Limit
- Upgrade Complete
- Upgrade Failed
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring Notifications.

entries.title: Default Filter Operator in Diagnostics
body: You can configure the default filter operator in the diagnostics settings.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring Diagnostics Settings.

entries.title: Deleting Disabled IdP Configurations for Authentication Service Admin Migration
body: Disabled admin IdP configurations that are migrated to Authentication Service will be permanently deleted after 30 days after migration. This only applies to admins that are subscribed to Authentication Service for users.
See image.
To learn more, see About IdP Configuration and What Is Authentication Service?

entries.title: Source IP Address Filter in User Activity Diagnostics
body: You can filter by Source IP Address in the user activity diagnostics.
See image.
To learn more, see Accessing User Activity Diagnostics.

entries.title: Scheduled VPN Service Edge Software Updates
body: This release includes the following enhancements for scheduling updates for VPN Service Edges:
- When adding a VPN Service Edge, you can schedule when a VPN Service Edge software update occurs to avoid service interruptions.
Zscaler strongly recommends scheduling updates to avoid service interruption when the device reboots during a software update.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring VPN Service Edges.
- You can edit the day and time the existing VPN Service Edge software is updated from the Edit VPN Service Edge drawer.
- See image.
- To learn more, see Editing VPN Service Edges.

- A banner also appears when logging in to the ZPA Admin Portal to recommend that you schedule updates for each VPN Service Edge to avoid service interruptions. If an update window is not set, the software updates on Sunday at 2:00 AM UTC.
- See image.
- To learn more, see About VPN Service Edges.

- An update was released for Private Cloud Controller to fix an issue where the Private Cloud Controller redirected users to the admin IdP (SSO) page instead of the user IdP (SSO).
- Support for remote troubleshooting (i.e., Support Information). To learn more, see Private Cloud Controller Support for Remote Troubleshooting.
- Support for backup and restore with database encryption. To learn more, see Backup Support for Private Cloud Controllers.
- Support for the Notifications service. To learn more, see Support for Private Cloud Controllers in the Notifications Service.
- Support for debugging commands to help with troubleshooting on the Private Cloud Controller. To learn more, see Troubleshooting Private Cloud Controllers.

- If you installed a Private Cloud Controller using the zpa-pcc.rpm file instead of a virtual image, manually update each Private Cloud Controller installed from an .rpm file in order to access debugging commands. To learn more, see Managing Deployed Private Cloud Controllers.
Your Private Cloud Controller will be updated based on your software update schedule as configured per Private Cloud Controller group.
To learn more, see Understanding Private Cloud Controller Software Upgrades.
# Manager Software Updates

A recommended update was released that ensures that if an OS upgrade is successful, and any underlying libraries that might be used by the Manager software are changed, the Manager software immediately restarts to make sure that there aren't any dependency errors. This release also includes an updated Private Cloud Controller RPM package for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.x. The Manager software version is 25.47.3.
To learn more, see Understanding the Manager Software.

entries.title: Azure Prebuilt Image Support for Network Connector
body: A new Network Connector image is available for Microsoft Azure that includes support for upcoming VPN redundancy features.
If you want to enable firewalld on a system running the Network Connector, you must perform additional steps to modify the firewall filter rule for VPN redundancy to work properly.
To learn more, see Network Connector Deployment Prerequisites and Network Connector Software by Platform.

entries.title: Manager Software Updates
body: A recommended update was released that ensures that if an OS upgrade is successful, and any underlying libraries that might be used by the Manager software are changed, the Manager software immediately restarts to make sure that there aren't any dependency errors. This release also includes updated App Connector and Private Service Edge for Private Access (ZPA) RPM packages for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8.x and 9.x.
You can download the Manager software for App Connectors or Private Service Edges from our repository. The Manager software version is 25.47.3.
To learn more, see Understanding the Manager Software.

entries.title: Resolved Issues
body: Resolved a rare root password expiration condition for 2024.11 and 2024.12 images when upgrading to the latest Manager software release.
To learn more, see Understanding the Manager Software.

entries.title: Extranet Support in Access Policies
body: An update was released to support using Extranet as the client type in Access Policies.
To learn more, see Extranet Client Type Support.

entries.title: Notifications Service Updates
body: The following updates were made to the notifications service:
- The Disk Space Exceeded Limit event threshold was increased from 1024 MB to 2048 MB.
- The Enrollment Certificate Expired and Enrollment Failed events were added for App Connectors and ZPA Private Service Edges.
To learn more, see Configuring Notifications.

entries.title: Privileged Approval Request Email Notifications
body: When you add or edit a privileged portal for Privileged Remote Access (PRA), you can add email addresses to notify administrators when a privileged approval request has been created, approved, and rejected. To use this feature, you must have an access policy that allows privileged approvals and a privileged portal policy with Request Approvals and Review Approvals enabled.
To learn more, see Configuring Privileged Portals.

- Support for setting Private Service Edge groups to be used exclusively for Business Continuity or Disaster Recovery. To learn more, see Business Continuity Updates.
Your ZPA Private Service Edge will be updated based on your software update schedule as configured per ZPA Private Service Edge group.
To learn more, see Understanding ZPA Private Service Edge Software Upgrades.
# Manager Software Updates

A recommended update was released that ensures that if an OS upgrade is successful, and any underlying libraries that might be used by the Manager software are changed, the Manager software immediately restarts to make sure that there aren't any dependency errors. This release also includes updated ZPA Private Service Edge RPM packages for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8.x and 9.x. The Manager software version is 25.46.3.
To learn more, see Understanding the Manager Software.

entries.title: VMware Prebuilt Image Update for Network Connector
body: An updated Network Connector image is available for VMware that includes support for upcoming VPN redundancy features.
If you want to enable firewalld on a system running the Network Connector, you must perform additional steps to modify the firewall filter rule for VPN redundancy to work properly.
To learn more, see Network Connector Deployment Prerequisites and Network Connector Software by Platform.

entries.title: Discovered Application Segments Update for Usage Insights
body: Discovered Host Count reports provide insight into the top 10 application segments by discovered host count, and are visible on the Application Segments Usage page.
See image.

In addition, a Discovered Application column was added to the table of a detailed report's CSV file to indicate if an application was discovered. Detailed reports can be downloaded from the Download CSV File window on the Application and User Group Relationships page.
See image.
To learn more, see Viewing Application Segments Usage and Viewing Application and User Group Relationships.

entries.title: Repository Update to Upgrade the Host OS to RHEL 9.6
body: A repository update that enhances virtual images is available for App Connectors, ZPA Private Service Edges, and Private Cloud Controllers. This update allows the host operating system (OS) to upgrade from Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) 9.4 and 9.5 to RHEL 9.6.
To learn more, see Updating the Host OS and Software Packages.

entries.title: SAML & SCIM Support for Usage Insights
body: You can select SAML and SCIM attributes in the Settings drawer of the Application and User Group Relationships page.
See image.
To learn more, see Viewing Application and User Group Relationships.

entries.title: AI-Powered Recommendations Updates
body: The Recommended Configuration drawer includes the following updates:

- The Users tab and Attributes tab for observed users includes a Total Users or Group Size column that lets you compare the number of observed users in the recommendation to the total number of users.
- The Users column was renamed to Observed Users to more easily identify observed versus total users.
See image.
To learn more, see About AI-Powered Recommendations for Application Segments.

entries.title: Disk Space Exceeded Limit Update in Events Diagnostics
body: An update was released that increases the Disk Space Exceeded Limit event threshold from 1024 MB to 2048 MB in Events Diagnostics.
See image.
To learn more, see Viewing and Managing Events Diagnostics.

entries.title: AppProtection API Protection Update
body: The following updates were made to the AppProtection API Protection feature:
- API Protection is included when configuring an application segment, by default.
- Some API Protection controls were moved to OWASP Predefined controls and ThreatLabZ controls.
- New filters were added to the AppProtection Diagnostics page: API Request, API Style, Auth type, Path, and Request method.
- The Recent API Activity widget was added to the API Protection dashboard.
To learn more, see Configuring Defined Application Segments, Configuring AppProtection Profiles, Accessing AppProtection Diagnostics, and Viewing the API Protection Dashboard.

entries.title: Enhanced Capabilities for API Protection
body: An update was released to support enhanced visibility and controls for API Protection.
To learn more, see Configuring AppProtection Profiles.

entries.title: Amazon Web Services Image Update for App Connector
body: A new AWS image is available for App Connector to support upcoming automated Manager software and OS security updates.
To learn more, see App Connector Deployment Guide for Amazon Web Services.

entries.title: Network Tag-Based Resource Groups for Microsegmentation
body: When configuring a resource group for Microsegmentation and adding cloud tags, you can now select the key "Exists." This allows the results to show if the tag itself exists at all or not, instead of matching that key to a value. When selected, the value field for the key is disabled.
Selecting this key option is especially useful when adding Google Cloud Platform (GCP) tags. It lets admins create resource groups based specifically on Google network tags.
See image.
To learn more, see About Resource Groups and Configuring Resource Groups.

entries.title: New Session Status Codes for Disconnections
body: If an App Connector or ZPA Private Service Edge was disconnected because of a planned restart, a redirect session status code is available on the User Activity Diagnostics page.
To learn more, see Understanding ZPA Session Status Codes.

body: This ZPA App Connector version includes the following updates:
- An update was released for App Connector that includes bug fixes, optimizations, and version enhancements.
- An update was released to support Kubernetes enhancements to improve container security. To learn more, see the App Connector Deployment Guide for Kubernetes.
Your App Connectors will be updated based on your software update schedule as configured per App Connector group.
To learn more, see Understanding App Connector Software Updates.
# Manager Software Updates
A recommended update was released that includes updated App Connector RPM packages for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8.x and 9.x. The Manager software version is 25.46.2.
To learn more, see Understanding the Manager Software.

entries.title: Network Connector Version 25.46.2
body: This Network Connector version includes the following updates:
- An update was released for Network Connector that includes bug fixes, optimizations, and version enhancements.

- Support for high availability and redundancy for Network Connector node failures and Network Connector to VPN Service Edge link failures using Border Gateway Protocols (BGPs). To learn more, see High Availability and Redundancy in VPN (for Legacy Apps).

- Support for upcoming functionality changes to provide Network Connector and Network Connector group details on the Diagnostics page. To learn more, see High Availability and Redundancy in VPN (for Legacy Apps).
To learn more, see Network Connector Software by Platform.
# Manager Software Updates
A recommended update was released that includes updated Private Cloud Controller RPM packages for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8.x and 9.x. The Manager software version is 25.46.2.
To learn more, see Understanding the Manager Software.

entries.title: Private Cloud Controller Version 25.46.2
body: This Private Cloud Controller version includes the following updates:
- An update was released for Private Cloud Controller that includes bug fixes, optimizations, and version enhancements.
- Support for forcing Private Cloud Controllers, App Connectors, and ZPA Private Service Edges into Business Continuity mode. To learn more, see Business Continuity Updates.
- Support for reporting the last policy/configuration and user sync times for Private Cloud Controllers. To learn more, see Business Continuity Updates.
Your Private Cloud Controllers will be updated based on your software update schedule as configured per Private Cloud Controller group.
To learn more, see Understanding Private Cloud Controller Software Upgrades.
# Manager Software Updates
A recommended update was released that includes updated Private Cloud Controller RPM packages for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.x. The Manager software version is 25.46.2.
To learn more, see Understanding the Manager Software.

entries.title: LAN IP Addresses and Subnets in VPN (for Legacy Apps)
body: This release includes an update to support adding LAN IP addresses and subnets for VPN (for Legacy Apps) network segments.
To learn more, see Multiple LAN IP Address and Subnet Support in VPN (for Legacy Apps).

entries.title: Manager Software Updates
body: A recommended update was released that includes updated App Connector and ZPA Private Service Edge RPM packages for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8.x and 9.x.
You can download the Manager software for App Connectors or ZPA Private Service Edges from our repository. The Manager software version is 25.46.2.
To learn more, see Understanding the Manager Software.

entries.title: Multimatch Validation for Application Segments
body: When Multimatch is enabled, a Multimatch Validation window appears for you to review any impacted application segments and conflicting features. Depending on the application segments selected, you might need to do one of the following:
- Edit an application segment and disable unsupported features before proceeding.
- Review conflicting features in a local Microtenant and select the checkboxes that appear to proceed.
- Contact the default administrator when Multimatch includes the default application segment.
- Cancel and disable Multimatch if an application segment belongs to another local tenant.
See image.
To learn more, see Using Application Segment Multimatch.

entries.title: ZPA Private Service Edge Version 25.46.2
body: This Private Service Edge version includes the following updates:
- An update was released for ZPA Private Service Edge that includes bug fixes, optimizations, and version enhancements.
- Support for setting Private Service Edge groups to be used exclusively for Business Continuity or Disaster Recovery. To learn more, see Business Continuity Updates.

Your ZPA Private Service Edge will be updated based on your software update schedule as configured per ZPA Private Service Edge group. To learn more, see Understanding ZPA Private Service Edge Software Upgrades.
# Manager Software Updates
A recommended update was released that includes updated ZPA Private Service Edge RPM packages for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8.x and 9.x. The Manager software version is 25.46.2.
To learn more, see Understanding the Manager Software.

entries.title: Cloud Service API Updates to Enable Multimatch in Bulk
body: The cloud service API includes the following new endpoints to extend programmatic access for application segment Multimatch:
- POST /customers/{customerId}/application/multimatchUnsupportedReferences
- PUT /customers/144118148382064640/application/bulkUpdateMultiMatch
To learn more, see Configuring Application Segment Multimatch Using API, Application Segment Management, and Using Application Segment Multimatch.

entries.title: Resolved Issues
body: A fix was released to update how data is processed for the Peak Zscaler Client Connector Redirections to Private Service Edges widget and the Zscaler Client Connector Redirections to Private Service Edges activity monitor widget in the Private Cloud Controllers dashboard.
To learn more, see Viewing the Private Cloud Controllers Dashboard.

entries.title: Update to AI-Powered Recommendations by Confidence % Widget
body: The AI-Powered Recommendations by Confidence % widget was updated to AI-Powered Recommendations by Attack Surface Reduction % in the Applications dashboard.
See image.
To learn more, see Viewing the Applications Dashboard.

entries.title: Kubernetes and OpenShift Enhancements for App Connector
body: This release provides the following updates for usability, security, and cross-platform compatibility improvements for the App Connector Helm charts:

- Improved container security includes fine-grained capability control options (minimal, full, custom). If CAP_NET_RAW is omitted in custom mode, a failsafe mechanism automatically injects it to ensure functionality. OpenShift deployments default to capabilityMode: full to maintain compatibility with platform restrictions.

- For App Connector version 25.45.1 or earlier, use only full mode to avoid unexpected behavior or compatibility issues. The minimal and custom capability modes are supported in App Connector versions later than 25.45.1.
- Namespace handling improvements include:
- The chart deployed in a Kubernetes cluster no longer auto-creates the specified namespace by default (e.g., zscaler-zpa). For OpenShift, the previous behavior is retained.

- Custom namespace support allows you to add --namespace and --create-namespace flags during installation. Namespaces are created by setting the createNamespace: true/false in values.yaml. Follow Helm's best practices for using these flags for consistent deployments.

- For K8s, if createNamespace: true, the previous behavior is retained for legacy automation and scripts for backward compatibility in Kubernetes. For OpenShift, the previous behavior is retained because the createNamespace flag isn't relevant, and the namespace is always created.

- Deployment-level labels are supported in values.yaml, enhancing chart customization for monitoring, alert routing, and resource filtering. Defaults are retained via the existing logic in _helpers.tpl for backward compatibility.

- A single, platform-aware chart structure supports both Kubernetes and OpenShift. It uses .Capabilities.APIVersions.Has to auto-detect and apply OpenShift-specific templates (e.g., SCC). This helps reduce duplication and simplify ongoing chart maintenance.
- Helm charts have been consolidated into a single, unified chart that supports both Kubernetes and OpenShift platforms with the following structure:
- The Helm Charts directory is unchanged:
- zscaler-et-dist/helm-charts/
- A new unified chart name has been created:
- zpa-app-connector
- The following chart directories have been deprecated:
- zscaler-et-dist/helm-charts/k8s/ zscaler-et-dist/helm-charts/openshift/
Zscaler recommends that you review and set the appropriate values in values.yaml:
- `capabilityMode` (minimal, full, custom)
- `createNamespace`
- `namespace`
- `labels`
To learn more, see App Connector Deployment Guide for Kubernetes and App Connector Deployment Guide for OpenShift.

entries.title: Multifile Support for Isolation in ZPA
body: Users can now upload multiple files simultaneously while in an isolated session. There is no minimum or maximum limit while uploading.
See image.
To learn more, see Transferring and Viewing Files in Isolation.

entries.title: AWS and Azure Image Support for Private Cloud Controllers
body: A new Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 Private Cloud Controller image is available in the AWS Marketplace and Microsoft Azure Marketplace.
To learn more, see Private Cloud Controller Software by Platform.

entries.title: Docker Image Updates
body: New Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 App Connector and ZPA Private Service Edge images are available for Docker. This release includes:
- Auto-updates for security patches during every container start or restart using micro-dnf.
- New Docker deployments that automatically include the latest available Manager software version and provide compatibility for seamless future Manager software and OS updates.
To learn more, see App Connector Software by Platform and ZPA Private Service Edge Software by Platform.

entries.title: Private Cloud Controller 25.45.2
body: This Private Cloud Controller software version addresses performance degradation observed during synchronization between Private Cloud Controllers when operating in disconnected mode from the Zero Trust Exchange (ZTE).
Your Private Cloud Controller will be updated based on your software update schedule as configured per Private Cloud Controller group.
To learn more, see Understanding Private Cloud Controller Software Upgrades.

entries.title: Provisioning Key Hardening in the ZPA Admin Portal
body: When creating a provisioning key for ZPA features such as App Connectors, Private Service Edges, Private Cloud Controllers, Network Connectors, or Machine Tunnels, you can choose to hide the provisioning key so it doesn't appear in the ZPA Admin Portal and can't be copied or downloaded for security purposes.
The View or Export Provisioning Key After Creation option must be enabled for Branch Connector and App Connector deployment.
See image.
To learn more, see About App Connector Provisioning Keys, About ZPA Private Service Edge Provisioning Keys, and About Private Cloud Controller Provisioning Keys.

entries.title: Event Logs for Agents and Resources
body: Microsegmentation now shows event logs for agent and resource diagnostics data. You can view a timestamp and priority level based on each log's information.
See image.
To learn more, see About Agents and About Resources.

entries.title: Managing Ignored ML Recommendations in Microsegmentation
body: You can now edit the list of ignored Machine Learning (ML) Recommendations for resource groups in Microsegmentation. This allows you to review the list of previously ignored recommendations and have the option to accept them.
To learn more, see About ML Recommendations for Resource Groups and About Resource Groups.

entries.title: ML Recommendations Dashboard Widget for Microsegmentation
body: The Overview Dashboard has a new widget to show Machine Learning (ML) Resource Group Recommendations for Microsegmentation. It provides a quick glimpse of enablement status and how many recommendations have been generated.
See image.
To learn more, see Viewing the Overview Dashboard.

entries.title: Usage Insights
body: Usage Insights provides you with actionable insights into an organization's usage patterns between users and applications.
See image.
To learn more, see About Usage Insights, Viewing Policy Usage, Viewing Policy Usage Details, and Viewing Application and User Group Relationships.

entries.title: Application Segments Usage
body: You can view or download Application Segments Usage reports from the ZPA Admin Portal to review insights into which application segments are actively used, and to provide visibility into which user groups are accessing the applications.
Application Segments Usage reports are only available to customers with the Segmentation add-on for eligible licenses.
See image.
To learn more, see Viewing Application Segments Usage and Viewing Application Segments Usage Details.

entries.title: AI-Powered Recommendations Updates
body: The following updates for AI-powered recommendations are available:

- When adding an application segment from an AI-powered recommendation, you can create an access policy rule at the Policies step. The rule is added to the middle of the rule order. Click Edit Policy if you need to move the rule higher or lower in the order.
- See image.
- To learn more, see Configuring AI-Powered Recommendations.
- The AI-Powered Recommendations page includes the following updates:
- Clicking an AI-powered recommendation in the Name column opens the Recommended Configuration details drawer.
- A new column was added that displays the total number of Recommended Users.
- See image.
- To learn more, see About AI-Powered Recommendations for Application Segments.
- The Recommended Configuration drawer includes the following updates:
- Information for recommended users and observed users appears when selecting a filter.
- A Groups or Attributes tab was added for both recommended and observed users that shows the SCIM groups, and attributes. You can also view the number of observed users for each SCIM group.
- An option to copy the list of recommended users is available to set up Group or Attribute configuration in your identity provider (IdP).
- An option to download a list of missing users is available from the warning message for those users missing the Group/Attribute configuration on your IdP side.

entries.title: Zscaler-Managed Business Continuity Cloud
body: The Zscaler-managed Business Continuity cloud is a fully managed Private Cloud solution that is built on the isolated and dedicated Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA) and Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) infrastructures. This ensures consistent cyber and data protection during critical failure events. For simplified operations and faster Business Continuity enablement, ZPA leverages the Business Continuity functionality that is deployed in a fully managed and hosted single-tenant environment.
Contact your Zscaler Account team for more information.
To learn more, see Understanding Business Continuity, Configuring Business Continuity Settings, and Understanding Zscaler-Managed Business Continuity Cloud.

entries.title: Cloud Service API Support for Onboarding Customers
body: The cloud service API includes the following new endpoints for administrator management, administrator role management, and client settings management:
- GET /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/administrators/{adminId}
- GET /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/administrators
- POST /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/administrators
- PUT /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/administrators/{adminId}
- DELETE /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/administrators/{adminId}
- GET /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/permissionGroups
- GET /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/roles
- GET /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/roles/{roleId}
- POST /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/roles
- PUT /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/roles/{roleId}
- DELETE /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/roles/{roleId}
- GET /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/clientSetting
- GET /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/clientSetting/all
- POST /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/clientSetting
- DELETE /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/clientSetting

Additionally, the following new endpoints are included to provision applications with all related objects, to generate self-signed enrollment (CA) certificates, and to generate certificate signing requests for enrollment certificates:
- POST /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/application/provision
- POST /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/enrollmentCert/selfsigned/generate
- POST /mgmtconfig/v1/admin/customers/{customerId}/enrollmentCert/csr/generate
To learn more about each endpoint, see Managing Administrators Using API, Managing Administrator Roles Using API, and Managing Client Settings Using API.

entries.title: ML Recommendations for Resource Groups in Microsegmentation

The recommendations are based off of analyzed resources that have multiple similarities, such as cloud user-defined tags, cloud environment metadata, and host data. Each ML recommendation also includes a Confidence Score, which determines the likelihood from 1 to 100 of how optimal it is for configuration. This can save admins time and effort in reviewing which individual resources should be grouped together.
See image.
To learn more, see About Resource Groups.

entries.title: Enhancing Security for Third-Party Clientless Access with ZPA and Chrome Enterprise Browser Integration

By leveraging Chrome's device posture signals, ZPA enforces granular security controls to manage clientless (third-party or contractor access) to private applications.
This integration verifies access to private applications and provides visibility for users that connect via the managed Chrome Enterprise browser based on the end user's access posture.

entries.title: VPN (for Legacy Apps)
body: ZPA can natively support a secondary Layer 3 network-based VPN tunnel for applications and services (e.g., VoIP or server-to-client) that require Layer 3 IP-based connectivity consistent with its Zero Trust security architecture and inside-out connection. From a single client for users and a single console for IT administrators, you can migrate to Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA) with ZPA and completely eliminate legacy VPNs. You can accelerate application modernization while retaining access for users during the transition.
To learn more, see Step-by-Step Configuration Guide for VPN (for Legacy Apps).

entries.title: STIG VM Image Updates for Microsoft Azure
body: Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 App Connector and Private Service Edge images that support Security Technical Implementation Guide (STIG) without requirements to disable password expiration are available for Microsoft Azure. The Azure STIG-hardened images released on December 12, 2024, required the password to be disabled. To verify if your image is affected, see Disabling Password Expiration for STIG-Hardened App Connector Images or Disabling Password Expiration for STIG-Hardened Private Service Edge Images.
The following guidelines have been disabled in the STIG images:
- Minimum and maximum password expiration
- Account expiration grace period after password expiration
- Account lock after three failed password attempts
- Writing all OS events to logs causes excessive disk usage in rare cases
To learn more, see ZPA App Connector Software by Platform or ZPA Private Service Edge Software by Platform.

entries.title: Update to Automatic Certificate Generation
body: An update to automatic certificate generation for AppProtection is available. By enabling AppProtection for an application segment and selecting an AppProtection enrollment (CA) certificate, you can automatically generate certificates to support AppProtection TLS inspection.

entries.title: AppProtection Control Exceptions
body: When configuring an AppProtection profile, you can add exceptions to OWASP predefined controls. After you create exceptions, you can review the exceptions under the OWASP predefined controls they are assigned to on the AppProtection Profile page.
To learn more, see About AppProtection Profiles and Configuring AppProtection Profiles.

entries.title: Client Connector for VDI Support
body: ZPA supports a new client type called Client Connector for VDI. Client Connector for VDI is a lightweight client for multi-session VDI environments. Admins can view and configure user-level ZPA policies to protect their multi-session ZPA users.

entries.title: Business Continuity Support
body: ZPA Business Continuity ensures continued access to applications for users in events where the reachability or availability of the ZPA cloud is affected. ZPA Business Continuity requires Business Continuity Settings, Private Clouds, and Private Cloud Controllers to be configured in the ZPA Admin Portal. Private Cloud Controller dashboard and diagnostics are available to help you monitor the health and diagnose issues for your organization's Private Cloud Controllers.
As part of this feature, the Private Cloud for Business Continuity field has been included when adding or editing an App Connector group or ZPA Private Service Edge group.

To learn more, see Understanding Business Continuity, Configuring Business Continuity Settings, About Private Clouds, About Private Cloud Controllers, Viewing the Private Cloud Controllers Dashboard, Accessing the Private Cloud Controller Status Diagnostics, Configuring App Connectors, and Configuring ZPA Private Service Edges.

entries.title: LSS Support for Private Cloud Controllers
body: An update was released in the Log Streaming Service (LSS) to provide stats for Private Cloud Controller status and metrics. The new log types can be selected when configuring a log receiver.
To learn more, see Understanding Private Cloud Controller Status Log Fields and Understanding Private Cloud Controller Metrics Log Fields.

entries.title: Microphone and Camera Functionality for Isolation Profiles in ZPA
body: Isolation allows microphone and camera functionality on the user's device while in an isolated browser. This can be enabled per isolation profile if Turbo Mode is also enabled.
See image.
To learn more, see Creating Isolation Profiles for ZPA.

entries.title: Role-Based Access Control for ZPA API
body: Granular role-based access control (RBAC) for ZPA API is available. You can select predefined roles or custom roles for API keys when adding them in the API Keys page of the ZPA Admin Portal. To enforce RBAC on all publicly available ZPA API operations, create a predefined or custom role in the ZPA Admin Portal, and then create an API client in the Authentication Service Admin Portal.
See image.
To learn more, see Understanding Role-Based Access Control for ZPA API, About API Key Management, Adding API Keys, About API Clients, and Adding an API Client.

entries.title: STIG VM Image Updates for AWS and GCP
body: Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 App Connector and Private Service Edge images that support Security Technical Implementation Guide (STIG) without requirements to disable password expiration are available for Amazon Web Services (AWS) and Google Cloud Platform (GCP). AWS and GCP STIG-hardened images released on November 24, 2024, required the password to be disabled. To verify if your image is affected, see Disabling Password Expiration for STIG-Hardened App Connector Images or Disabling Password Expiration for STIG-Hardened Private Service Edge Images.
The following guidelines have been disabled in the STIG images:
- Minimum and maximum password expiration
- Account expiration grace period after password expiration
- Account lock after three failed password attempts
- Writing all OS events to logs causes excessive disk usage in rare cases
To learn more, see ZPA App Connector Software by Platform or ZPA Private Service Edge Software by Platform.

entries.title: Microsegmentation Admin Config Resource Type Update
body: A new resource type for Microsegmentation Admin Config was added to the Audit Logs page.
See image.
To learn more, see About Audit Logs and About Audit Log Fields.

entries.title: Platform Information Available for User Activity Log
body: An update was made to support the platform where Zscaler Client Connector is installed in the User Activity Logs.
To learn more, see Accessing User Activity Diagnostics.

entries.title: Extranet Application Support Available on Cloud & Branch Connectors
body: Extranet Application Support is available on ZPA Cloud Connectors and Branch Connectors.
To learn more, see About Extranet, About Cloud Connectors, and About Branch Connectors.

entries.title: ZPA Private Service Edge Version 25.42.5
body: An update was released for ZPA Private Service Edge that includes bug fixes, optimizations, and version enhancements.

Your ZPA Private Service Edge will be updated based on your software update schedule as configured per ZPA Private Service Edge group. To learn more, see Understanding ZPA Private Service Edge Software Upgrades.
