body: This ZPA Private Service Edge version includes a fix to address an issue where using multiple IdPs with one entity ID being a substring of the other would configure an incorrect IdP for the user.

Your ZPA Private Service Edge will be updated based on your software update schedule as configured per ZPA Private Service Edge group. To learn more, see About ZPA Private Service Edge Software Upgrades.

entries.title: Comprehensive App Connector Stats
body: An update was released in the Log Streaming Service (LSS) to provide comprehensive App Connector stats. The new log type can be selected when configuring a log receiver.

entries.title: App Connector Release 21.255.2
body: This App Connector software version includes the following updates:
- An update was released to the Log Streaming Service (LSS) to provide comprehensive App Connector stats. The new log type can be selected when configuring a log receiver.
- An update was released for App Connectors that allows the reporting of CPU time stolen from the VM by a Hypervisor.
Your App Connectors will be updated based on your software update schedule as configured per App Connector group. To learn more, see About App Connector Software Updates.
# Resolved Issues
An update was released to address a high memory consumption issue in App Connectors when handling ICMP probes.

entries.title: Cloud and Admin Portal Updates
body: The following updates were made to the Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) Cloud and Admin Portal:

- An update was made that improves the lookup service in the Log Streaming Service (LSS) to add the GID to name translations to show ClientZEN and ConnectorZEN names correctly when traffic is processed by a ZPA Private Service Edge.
- An update was released for App Connectors and ZPA Private Service Edges that allows the reporting of CPU steal time from the VM by a Hypervisor.

- An update was released to address an issue where the ZPA Public Service Edge or Private Service Edge rejected the application access request coming from the deactivated user, or from a user whose active status is not synced via SCIM.

entries.title: ZPA Private Service Edge Version 21.255.1
body: This ZPA Private Service Edge version includes the following update:
- An update was released for ZPA Private Service Edges that allows the reporting of CPU steal time from the VM by a Hypervisor.

Your ZPA Private Service Edge will be updated based on your software update schedule as configured per ZPA Private Service Edge group. To learn more, see About ZPA Private Service Edge Software Upgrades.

entries.title: App Connector Release 21.224.3
body: An update was released to address an issue where App Connectors that have health-enabled UDP applications, or ICMP-enabled applications, would experience high memory consumption in ICMP probes.
Your App Connectors will be updated based on your software update schedule as configured per App Connector group. To learn more, see About App Connector Software Updates.

entries.title: ZPA Support with ZDX
body: Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) supports Digital Experience (ZDX) so you can measure performance in the cloud path for internal applications. Data is encrypted and stored at rest before being shipped to the ZDX infrastructure using HTTPS. Zscaler recommends App Connector specifications and sizing requirements for ZDX deployments.
To learn more, see Monitoring the Users Dashboard.

entries.title: ZPA API Improvements
body: The following improvements were made to the Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) cloud service APIs:
- New management APIs are now available to manage App Connectors, App Connector Groups, Service Edges, Service Edge Groups, and Log Streaming Service (LSS) configurations.
- New prerequisite APIs for enrollment certificates, provisioning keys, and to get version profiles, client types, status codes, and LSS formats are added.
- A new API to reorder policy rules is added.
- The endpoints to get all browser access (BA) certificates, IdPs, posture profiles, trusted networks, and SAML attributes are now deprecated, and new APIs with pagination are provided.
- API endpoints specific to a policy (global/reauth/bypass) are deprecated and replaced by a generic API that takes policyType as a parameter.

- The port range configuration for the application segment has been enhanced for more readability. The tcpPortRanges and udpPortRanges fields are deprecated and replaced with tcpPortRange and udpPortRange.
To learn more, see the ZPA API Developer's Guide.
# Resolved Issues
An update was released to address an issue where creating or modifying an access policy rule would return an invalid SCIM attribute error.

entries.title: App Connector Release 21.224.1
body: This App Connector software version includes the following update:
- An enhancement was made that optimizes the CPU usage by reducing the frequency of journalctl logs being processed.
Your App Connectors will be updated based on your software update schedule as configured per App Connector group. To learn more, see About App Connector Software Updates.

entries.title: Cloud Update
body: An update was released that optimizes the CPU usage for App Connectors by reducing the frequency of journalctl logs being processed.

entries.title: Cloud Browser Isolation Integration with ZPA
body: Cloud Browser Isolation is now integrated with Zscaler Private Access (ZPA). This allows ZPA admins to configure policies for isolating web application traffic. To learn more see, About Isolation Policies.
Organizations can now configure isolation profiles in the Zscaler Cloud Browser Isolation Portal for both ZIA and ZPA. To learn more, see Creating a ZPA Isolation Profile for Cloud Browser Isolation.

entries.title: ZPA Private Service Edge Version 21.224.2
body: This ZPA Private Service Edge version includes a fix to address an issue where terminating existing ZPA Microtunnels (M-Tunnels) on timeout causes interrupted connections.

Your ZPA Private Service Edge will be updated based on your software update schedule as configured per ZPA Private Service Edge group. To learn more, see About ZPA Private Service Edge Software Upgrades.

entries.title: New Filters for User Activity Trends
body: An update was released to include new filters for User Activity trends. You can now filter by application domain and port, connection status code, dispatcher ID, machine tunnel, user client type, and username. To learn more, see About User Activity Diagnostics.

entries.title: SCIM Sync Logs
body: SCIM Sync Logs are now available in the ZPA Admin Portal under SCIM Management. Operations that change the state of the users and groups are presented on the SCIM Sync Logs page. To learn more, see About SCIM Sync Logs.

entries.title: ZPA Private Service Edge Version 21.172.5
body: This ZPA Private Service Edge version includes a fix to address an issue where the policy would fail to load for the customer if they never connected to the ZPA Public Service Edge.

Your ZPA Private Service Edge will be updated based on your software update schedule as configured per ZPA Private Service Edge group. To learn more, see About ZPA Private Service Edge Software Upgrades.

entries.title: New User Activity Filters
body: An update was released to include new user activity filter types. You can now filter by connection type and forwarded ZPA Public Service Edge or ZPA Private Service Edge name. To learn more, see About User Activity Diagnostics.

entries.title: Admin Portal Enhancement
body: An update was released that improves the user experience in the Admin Portal when deleting application segments that reference segment groups or policies. If an application segment is linked to any policy, an admin must remove the link to delete the application segment. To learn more, see About Applications.

entries.title: Version Profiles
body: ZPA now supports the ability to configure a version profile when adding or editing an App Connector group or ZPA Private Service Edge group in the ZPA Admin Portal.

entries.title: App Connector Health Visualization
body: The App Connector dashboard now includes different metrics, new widgets, and expanded visualization to allow you to better monitor the health of your organization's App Connectors and diagnose issues. To learn more, see About App Connector Dashboard.

entries.title: SCIM Service Schema and Related API Enhancements
body: The following issues were resolved:
- An update was released to address an issue where a SCIM user attribute returned an incorrect type.
- An update was released to address an issue to remove a duplicate group attribute and correct the reference URL for the group attribute to match the schema when running a GET request for SCIM APIs.
- An update was released to address an issue where a name sub attribute was not being returned in the schema of the SCIM APIs.
# Resolved Issues
An update was released to address an issue that caused performance degradation in ZPA Public Service Edges while processing connection requests.

entries.title: TCP Communication Sockets
body: You can now enable App Connectors to maintain TCP communication sockets using the TCP Keepalive socket option when adding or editing Segment Groups in the ZPA Admin Portal. To learn more, see Networking Deployed App Connectors.

entries.title: ZPA Admin Portal Updates
body: The following updates were made to the Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) Cloud and Admin Portal:

- The Users Dashboard features several updates to the Recent Users and Current Connected Users widgets to view machine tunnel connections in real-time and during selected periods. To learn more, see About the Users Dashboard.

- An update was made to the ZPA Admin Portal which allows you to enable the termination of users’ running application sessions upon re-authentication according to timeout policy. This setting supports termination of existing ZPA Microtunnels (M-Tunnels) upon authentication expiry, or upon policy change denying access mentioned in ZPA Private Service Edge Version 21.172.1. To learn more, see About Timeout Policy.

entries.title: App Connector Release 21.172.1
body: This App Connector software version includes the following updates:
- An update was released that allows App Connectors to maintain TCP communication sockets using the TCP Keepalive socket option in support for future functionality changes.
- An enhancement was made that improves the App Connector's efficiency for reporting Application registration information.
- An update was released for App Connectors that changes the DNS endpoint for log collection.
Your App Connectors will be updated based on your software update schedule as configured per App Connector group. To learn more, see About App Connector Software Updates.

entries.title: Cloud and Admin Portal Updates
body: The following updates were made to the Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) Cloud and Admin Portal:
- An update was released that allows termination of existing ZPA Microtunnels (M-Tunnels) in preparation for functionality changes.
- An update was released for ZPA Public Service Edges and ZPA Private Service Edges to support geofencing at a sub-cloud level.
- An update was released that allows App Connectors to maintain TCP communication sockets using the TCP Keepalive socket option in support for future functionality changes.
- An enhancement was made that improves the App Connector's efficiency for reporting Application registration information.
- An update was released for App Connectors that changes the DNS endpoint for log collection.

entries.title: ZPA Private Service Edge Version 21.172.1
body: This ZPA Private Service Edge version includes the following updates:
- An update was made that supports the termination of existing ZPA Microtunnels (M-Tunnels) in preparation for functionality changes.
- An update was released for ZPA Public Service Edges and ZPA Private Service Edges to support geofencing at a sub-cloud level.

Your ZPA Private Service Edge will be updated based on your software update schedule as configured per ZPA Private Service Edge group. To learn more, see About ZPA Private Service Edge Software Upgrades.

entries.title: Cloud Updates
body: The following updates were made to the Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) Cloud:
- An update was released to address an issue that caused performance degradation in ZPA Public Service Edges while processing connection requests.
- An update was released to address an issue where some application traffic intended for Source IP Anchoring was going to ZIA instead.

entries.title: Cloud Update
body: An update was released to address an issue with IP caching that caused connections timeout errors for some users accessing applications via Browser Access.

entries.title: ZPA Public Service Edge Update
body: An update was released to address an issue with disconnected SIPA clients upon ZPA Public Service Edge restart.

entries.title: Cloud Update
body: An update was released to address an issue with authentication through Identity Providers (IdPs) that send an IP address in the subject confirmation data of a SAML response.

entries.title: Service Provider Certificate Rotation
body: You can now rotate the service provider certificate for your identity providers (IdPs) in the ZPA Admin Portal. This option is available when editing an IdP by selecting a different certificate in the User SP Certificate Rotation or Admin SP Certificate Rotation field.
This field may show as SP Certificate Rotation if the original IdP was configured to use Both (i.e., admin and user SSO) when that option was available.
Making this change may require additional changes to the IdP. To learn more, see Managing a Service Provider Certificate Rotation.

entries.title: ZPA Admin Portal Enhancement
body: You can now unlock administrators and API Clients who have failed authentication three times in the ZPA Admin Portal. To learn more, see About Administrators and About API Keys.

entries.title: App Connector Release 21.146.3
body: This App Connector software version includes an update to address an issue of high CPU usage on App Connectors.
Your App Connectors will be updated based on your software update schedule as configured per App Connector group. To learn more, see About App Connector Software Updates.

entries.title: Cloud Update
body: An update was released to address an issue for ZPA Public Service Edges and ZPA Private Service Edges due to ICMP application transactions issued during policy checks.

entries.title: ZPA Private Service Edge Version 21.146.2
body: This ZPA Private Service Edge version includes a fix to address an issue for ZPA Public Service Edges and ZPA Private Service Edges due to ICMP application transactions issued during policy checks.

Your ZPA Private Service Edge will be updated based on your software update schedule as configured per ZPA Private Service Edge group. To learn more, see About ZPA Private Service Edge Software Upgrades.

entries.title: App Connector Release 21.146.1
body: This App Connector version includes the following update:
- Improvements were made to support ZPA Cloud changes.
Your App Connectors will be updated based on your software update schedule as configured per App Connector group. To learn more, see About App Connector Software Updates.

entries.title: ZPA Private Service Edge Support for SCIM Policies
body: ZPA Private Service Edges now support SCIM for policies. To learn more, see About ZPA Private Service Edges.

entries.title: Cloud and Admin Portal Updates for ICMP
body: ICMP functionality is now available. End users can now use ping to determine reachability to internal applications via an IP address or a hostname. This functionality will appear visible in the ZPA Admin Portal, but it requires end-user devices to upgrade to Zscaler Client Connector version 3.5 for the Windows platform.

When setting up an Application Segment, you can now choose whether the Zscaler Client Connector will allow ICMP communication with the App Connector. To learn more, see Configuring Application Segments.
You can also use an ICMP protocol to filter your Live Logs and User Activity Diagnostic logs.
# Resolved Issues
An update was released to address an issue where the App Connector page in the ZPA Admin Portal was showing Uptime as Not Available due to incorrect information reported by the App Connector.

entries.title: App Connector Release 21.145.1
body: This App Connector software version includes the following updates:
- Improvements were made to different components to ensure better logging and reporting.

- A new root central authority (CA) certificate for Zscaler software repositories was added to ensure App Connectors can auto-update when the current Zscaler software repository TLS certificate renews. This requires a manual RPM update of the App Connector. To learn more, see Managing Deployed App Connectors.
Your App Connectors will be updated based on your software update schedule as configured per App Connector group. To learn more, see About App Connector Software Updates.

entries.title: ZPA Private Service Edge Version 21.146.1
body: This ZPA Private Service Edge version includes the following update:
- ZPA Private Service Edges now support SCIM for policies. To learn more, see About ZPA Private Service Edges.

Your ZPA Private Service Edge will be updated based on your software update schedule as configured per ZPA Private Service Edge group. To learn more, see About ZPA Private Service Edge Software Upgrades.

entries.title: Admin Portal Enhancements
body: The number of DNS search domains that can be added as suffixes to application names is now limited to 50. Customers that currently have more than the limit will not be able to add more DNS suffixes, but you will be able to replace existing ones. To learn more, see Ranges and Limits.

entries.title: Updated Package for App Connectors in AWS and Microsoft Azure Marketplace
body: An updated package for App Connectors is available in AWS and Microsoft Azure Marketplace. You are not required to update existing App Connectors in AWS and Azure. The updated package is only required for new instances of the App Connector. The package includes recently released updates for Centos 7.
# Resolved Issues
An update was released to disable GSS authentication in App Connectors in order to address a Redhat user enumeration vulnerability.

entries.title: Export Application Segment Configurations
body: You can now export your organization’s application segment configurations from the ZPA Admin Portal. To learn more, see About Applications.
See image.

entries.title: Cloud Update
body: An update was released to address an issue where logs on the Private Service Edge Status Diagnostics page were not appearing in the ZPA Admin Portal.

entries.title: Cloud and Admin Portal Updates
body: The following updates were made to the Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) Cloud and Admin Portal:
- An update was released to address an issue where in certain situations single sign-on to the ZPA Admin Portal was not successful.

- An update was released to address an issue where certain incomplete access policy rules created using the ZPA Public API prevented the ZPA Admin Portal from correctly displaying the corresponding Access Policy configurations.

entries.title: Cloud Updates
body: The following updates were made to the Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) Cloud:
- An enhancement was made to improve the efficiency of processing policies in ZPA.
- Improvements were made to different components to ensure the security and integrity of the ZPA cloud infrastructure.
- An improvement was released to limit the Microtunnel ​​​​​(M-Tunnel) requests per user to 100/second.

entries.title: Cloud Update
body: An update was released to address an issue where ZPA was incorrectly processing the API gateway for EU customers.

entries.title: App Connector Release 21.104.1
body: This App Connector software version includes the following updates:
- Improvements were made to different components to ensure the security and integrity of the ZPA cloud infrastructure.
- An update was released to address an issue with data connections to ZPA Private Service Edges that are proxied via App Connectors.
- An update was released to limit App Connector logs to 64 MB.
Your App Connectors will be updated based on your software update schedule as configured per App Connector group. To learn more, see About App Connector Software Updates.

entries.title: Cloud Update
body: An update was made to exclude machine tunnels for Recent Users and Connected Users counts in the Users Dashboard.

entries.title: Cloud Update
body: An update was released to address an issue where customerId was not correctly interpreted for certain ZPA APIs.

entries.title: Cloud Updates
body: The following updates were made to the Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) Cloud:

- After enabling SCIM Attributes for Policy for an IdP in the ZPA Admin Portal, ZPA now requires a user to reauthenticate in Zscaler Client Connector. ZPA will only evaluate policies with SCIM criteria for this user after the user successfully reauthenticates. To learn more, see Configuring an IdP for Single Sign-On
- An update was made to address an issue where the ZPA API was not fetching the records by customerId.

entries.title: User Experience Enhancements
body: The Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) Admin Portal will now provide a warning to alert Admins when the current number of applications definitions is close to 6000. The maximum number of supported application definitions is 6000.

entries.title: Cloud Updates
body: An update was released to address an issue related to communication between ZPA Private Service Edges and ZPA Public Service Edges that caused the ZPA Public Service Edges to experience intermittent degradation.

entries.title: SCIM API Support
body: The SCIM Service in ZPA was enhanced to return a list of groups for a specific user.

entries.title: Cloud Updates
body: The ZPA Cloud update includes improvements to infrastructure that supports TLS encryption across different components.
# Resolved Issues
The following issues were resolved:
- An update was released to address an issue where ZPA Public Service Edges were sending additional messages to the Zscaler Client Connector after authentication was achieved.
- An update was released to address an issue where the country code for App Connector groups were not appearing in the App Connector Status Logs.
- An update was released to address an issue where the search functionality was unavailable when editing an Application Segment in the ZPA Admin Portal.
- An update was released to address an issue in the ZPA Admin Portal that prevented deleting or moving existing Access Policy rules that have names containing special characters.

entries.title: App Connector Release 21.67.1
body: This App Connector software version includes the following updates:
- The file descriptor limit for the LimitNOFILE value in the systemd file was raised from 100,000 to 500,000 for the App Connector process.
- Improvements were made to the infrastructure that supports TLS encryption across different components.

- An update was released to address an issue where latitude and longitude information for App Connector Groups was not reported to ZPA's path selection service if the application segments referencing these App Connector Groups were configured for On Access health reporting or when health reporting was disabled.
- An update was released to address an issue where the country code for App Connector groups were not appearing in the App Connector Status Logs.
- An update was released to support App Connector deployments on Docker platforms. To learn more, see the App Connector Deployment Guide for Docker.
Your App Connectors will be updated based on your software update schedule as configured per App Connector group. To learn more, see About App Connector Software Updates.

entries.title: Admin Portal Improvements
body: An update was released to address an issue where an error message would appear when searching by SCIM User Name on the SCIM Groups page in the ZPA Admin Portal.

entries.title: ZPA API
body: Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) now supports customer facing APIs for managing application segments and policies. To learn more, see About ZPA API.
API access requires an API key, which you can add in the ZPA Admin Portal. To learn more, see About API Keys.
# Admin Portal Improvements
Zscaler now allows the termination of Admin sessions created using an API key or via the Admin Portal. To learn more see, About Client Sessions.
# Cloud Updates

Zscaler has made enhancements to the ZPA Cloud for improving load balancing of application requests across App Connectors. As part of this enhancement, ZPA will account for CPU, memory, and UDP port consumption for each eligible App Connector, and it will try to select an App Connector with lower utilization by using a probability mass function (PMF) algorithm.

entries.title: Cloud Updates
body: The following updates were made to the Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) Cloud:
- ZPA Public Service Edges now cache App Connector selection decisions based on earlier application requests.
- ZPA Private Service Edges now support Machine Tunnels. To learn more, see About Machine Tunnels.

entries.title: App Connector Release 21.51.1
body: This App Connector software version includes the following updates:
- ZPA Public Service Edges now cache App Connector selection decisions based on earlier application requests. These changes require an update to the App Connector software.
Your App Connectors will be updated based on your software update schedule as configured per App Connector group. To learn more, see About App Connector Software Updates.

entries.title: ZPA Private Service Edge Version 21.51.1
body: This ZPA Private Service Edge version includes the following update:
- ZPA Private Service Edges now support Machine Tunnels. To learn more, see About Machine Tunnels.

Your ZPA Private Service Edge will be updated based on your software update schedule as configured per ZPA Private Service Edge group. To learn more, see About ZPA Private Service Edge Software Upgrades.

entries.title: Admin Portal Improvements
body: The Access Policy, Client Forwarding Policy, and Timeout Policy pages now include the ability to filter the tables by rule criteria. To learn more, see About Access Policy, About Timeout Policy, and About Client Forwarding Policy.

entries.title: Admin Portal Enhancements
body: When setting up an App Connector, you can now configure the App Connector group to perform IPv4 only DNS resolution checks for applications. To learn more, Configuring App Connectors.
# Cloud Updates
The following updates were made to the Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) Cloud:
- The Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) Cloud now includes enhancements that improve the processing of browser access application requests when access policies use SCIM attributes.
- The Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) Cloud now includes an enhancement that improves the App Connector’s efficiency for reporting Application reachability information.
# Resolved Issues
The following issues were resolved:
- An update was released to address an issue where scrolling to the end of the Users Blocked By Policies list in the Users dashboard resulted in the list resetting to no users.
- An update was released to improve the accuracy of the connection setup time (i.e., Connection: Setup Time) in Diagnostics.
- An update was released to improve the processing of App Connector Group configurations in Access Policies with respect to the App Connector selection.
- An update was released to improve how an App Connector verifies its permissions to specific directories on the host.

entries.title: App Connector Release 21.46.1
body: This App Connector software version includes the following updates:
- When setting up an App Connector, you can now configure the App Connector group to perform IPv4 only DNS resolution checks for applications. To learn more, Configuring App Connectors.
- An update was released to improve how an App Connector verifies its permissions to specific directories on the host.
- The Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) Cloud now includes an enhancement that improves the App Connector’s efficiency for reporting Application reachability information.
- An update was released to improve memory management in App Connector software related to termination of Application sessions.
- An update was released to more accurately capture the time it takes an App Connector to establish the connection to the application server.
- An update was released to improve the processing of App Connector Group configuration in Access Policy with respect to App Connector selection.
Your App Connectors will be updated based on your software update schedule as configured per App Connector group. To learn more, see About App Connector Software Updates.

entries.title: Cloud Updates
body: The following issues were resolved:
- An update was released to address an issue that caused performance degradation in ZPA Public Service Edges due to high memory consumption.
- An update was released to address an issue where, in certain cases, ZPA Public Service Edges did not learn the entire application configuration information.

entries.title: Trend Charts
body: The Diagnostics section of the Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) Admin Portal now displays trend charts for User Activity logs. To learn more, see About User Activity Diagnostics.

entries.title: Pre-Windows Login
body: Zscaler Private Access now supports a new client type called Machine Tunnel. By using a machine tunnel, a user’s Windows device can be configured to access internal applications even when the device’s Zscaler Client Connector is not connected to ZPA. To learn more, see About Machine Groups.

To use this feature, you need to configure Machines groups and Machine Provisioning keys in the ZPA Admin Portal and add keys to Zscaler Client Connector profile rules for Windows. It also requires the Zscaler Client Connector version 3.2 for Windows at the minimum.
# Resolved Issues

A fix was released to address an issue where ZPA incorrectly processed configurations for a Log Receiver set up for the Log Streaming Service (LSS) and prevented the user from accessing the Log Receiver over ZPA.

entries.title: App Connector Release 21.40.1
body: This App Connector software version includes updates to address an issue where App Connectors experienced performance degradation when processing traffic for LSS.
Your App Connectors will be updated based on your software update schedule as configured per App Connector group. To learn more, see About App Connector Software Updates.

entries.title: Cloud Updates
body: The following updates were made to the Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) Cloud:
- An update was released to the improve the efficiency of a database service used by ZPA.

- A fix was released to address an issue that caused ZPA to send User Activity logs with certain Session Codes to a log receiver, even when these Session Codes were excluded in the Log Receiver configuration.

entries.title: ZPA Private Service Edge Version 21.23.2
body: This ZPA Private Service Edge version includes a fix to address an issue where certain users were unable to connect to a ZPA Private Service Edge when ZPA policy rules were configured with SCIM attributes.

Your ZPA Private Service Edge will be updated based on your software update schedule as configured per ZPA Private Service Edge group. To learn more, see About ZPA Private Service Edge Software Upgrades.

entries.title: Time Zone Selection
body: The Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) Admin Portal now allows you to choose a time zone in your account settings. Timestamps and time interval selection in the ZPA Admin Portal will reflect your local or chosen time zone. To learn more, see About the ZPA Admin Portal.
# Session Pinning

The ZPA Admin Portal now includes a Session Pin setting when creating admins. This setting ensures that a session token connects to the user to whom it was issued. It is enabled by default. To learn more, see Configuring ZPA Administrators.
See image.
# Admin Portal Improvements
For the Time Range filter on the Application Dashboard and Users Dashboard, you can now set a Custom Range in increments of 5 minutes.

entries.title: Cloud Updates
body: An update was released to address an issue where, in certain conditions, users were unable to connect to Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) if SCIM attributes were configured as criteria in ZPA policy rules.

entries.title: Admin Portal Improvements
body: The Health dashboard now identifies disconnected ZPA Private Service Edges with a Disconnected label below the ZPA Private Service Edge.

entries.title: Cloud Updates
body: Zscaler has made load balancing enhancements to improve transmission of logs from ZPA Public Service Edges to ZPA's log infrastructure.

entries.title: Country Code for App Connectors
body: Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) automatically populates the country code for an App Connector’s location based on the address specified for the App Connector group. ZPA will now use the country code to determine an App Connector’s location for App Connector selection decisions. To learn more, see Configuring App Connectors.

As part of enabling this functionality across ZPA, the Zscaler Operations team will perform a one time update to the ZPA database. This will result in an Audit Log corresponding to the Admin ID showing [user]@root.zscaler.com. It is available to review in an organization’s tenant under Administration > Audit Logs. To learn more, see About Audit Logs.

entries.title: Resolved Issues
body: The following issues were resolved:

- A fix was released to address an issue where, in certain situations, ZPA's Path Selection micro-service did not correctly process application reachability information that was reported by App Connectors.
- A fix was released to address an issue related to processing SCIM attributes that, for certain users, prevented Zscaler Client Connector from setting up a connection to ZPA.

entries.title: Resolved Issues
body: A fix was released to address an issue that prevented some users from connecting to ZPA due to the way SCIM was processing the username formats.

entries.title: SCIM Policies
body: You can now configure access policies, timeout policies, and client forwarding policies with SCIM attributes and SCIM groups as criteria.

To allow the use of SCIM attributes and SCIM groups in policies, there is the new SCIM Attributes and Groups for Policy setting to enable when creating an identity provider. To learn more, see Configuring an IdP for Single Sign-On.
As part of SCIM policy changes, there are new session status codes related to the disabling of users by SCIM. To learn more, see About ZPA Session Status Codes.
# Admin Portal Improvements
The Health dashboard now identifies disabled App Connectors with a label below the App Connector.
See image.
A maximum of 100 names can be specified in the filters for App Connector: Name and Service Edge: Name (Public/Private) on the diagnostic pages.
# Resolved Issues
The following issues were resolved:
- A fix was released to address an issue where the Admin UI was not detecting duplicate names when creating application segments.
- A fix was released to address an issue where the Last Updated timestamp on the SCIM Group page was not accurately displayed.
- A fix was released to address an issue where hover over text in the ZPA Admin Portal would remain on the screen after the cursor moved.

- A fix was released to address an issue where the list of Current Connected Users on the Users dashboard page showed the “No current connected users at this time” message at the end of a list of users.

- A fix was released to address an issue where ZPA Public Service Edges and ZPA Private Service Edges experienced intermittent performance degradation while processing DNS resolutions during application access.
- A fix was released to address an issue where the ZPA Admin Portal prevented the creation of new App Connector Provisioning Keys when configuring an App Connector.
- A fix was released to address an issue that prevented the creation of an IdP for admin SSO if the SCIM Sync setting was enabled.

entries.title: Resolved Issues
body: A fix was released to address an issue where ZPA Public Service Edges and ZPA Private Service Edges experienced service degradation when processing connections.

entries.title: Admin Portal Improvements
body: The Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) Admin Portal was updated to prevent the execution of malicious payload in the UI.

entries.title: App Connector Release 20.140.2
body: This App Connector software version includes an update for reporting application health. In order to prevent App Connector performance degradation during application discovery, App Connectors perform application reachability checks for a maximum of 6000 applications for Application Segments configured with Health Reporting set to On Access.
There is no limit to the number of applications that an App Connector is capable of monitoring for Application Segments configured for Health Reporting set to Continuous.
Your App Connectors will be updated based on your software update schedule as configured per App Connector group. To learn more, see About App Connector Software Updates.

entries.title: Cloud Updates
body: The Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) Cloud will now stop health reporting if the number of applications that an App Connector is currently monitoring for reachability is greater than 6000 at one time.

entries.title: Multiple Posture Profile Condition Sets
body: You can now configure access policies, timeout policies, and client forwarding policies with multiple posture profile condition sets. You can add up to 10 condition sets.
See image.

entries.title: Admin Portal Improvements
body: The Diagnostic pages have been enhanced to display additional transactions by just scrolling on the page. By default, the first 20 transactions are displayed.

entries.title: Support for Encrypted Log Delivery to a Log Receiver
body: You can now configure the ZPA Log Streaming Service (LSS) to encrypt logs between the LSS App Connector and a log receiver using TLS encryption. To learn more, see Configuring Log Receiver.
# Browser Access Log Fields
The Browser Access log fields Origin and CorsToken are now part of the default log template. To learn more, see About Browser Access Log Fields.

entries.title: Resolved Issues
body: A fix was released to address an issue where, under certain circumstances, new App Connectors cannot be registered to a customer's ZPA tenant.

entries.title: App Connector Release 20.121.1
body: This App Connector software version includes updates that:
- Enable Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) Log Streaming Service (LSS) to encrypt logs between the LSS App Connector and a log receiver using TLS encryption.

- Allow the software to reuse open UDP sockets for initiating connections to application servers instead of opening a new UDP socket for an application connection. This change reduces the number of UDP ports that are used by an App Connector to open connections to application servers, which reduces the possibility of UDP port exhaustion on the App Connector host.
- Address an issue where the App Connector software experienced degradation when processing traffic for applications over UDP.
Your App Connectors will be updated based on your software update schedule as configured per App Connector group. To learn more, see About App Connector Software Updates.

entries.title: Cloud Updates
body: The Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) Cloud now includes an enhancement to speed up policy processing related to application access.

entries.title: Browser Access Enhancements
body: Starting with this release Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) will forward authenticated CORS requests to an App Connector by setting the Access-Control-Allow-Origin header to null for the browser to process the response. For unauthenticated CORS requests, ZPA will redirect them to an authentication domain and set the Origin header to null. To learn more, see About Browser Access.
The current supported browsers for CORS requests are:
- Firefox 81.0
- Chrome 64_65
- Google Chrome 86.0.4240.75
- Microsoft Edge 86.0.622.43
- Safari 12.0
- Safari 13.0
There are two new Browser Access log fields, Origin and CorsToken, that can be added to a Custom Log Template.To learn more, see About Browser Access Log Fields.
# Resolved Issues
The following issues were resolved:
- A fix was released to address an issue where, under certain circumstances, Administrators were unable to edit Access Policies in the ZPA Admin Portal.
- A fix was released to address an issue where, for certain browsers, the authentication cookies issued by ZPA did not have the samesite attribute set.

entries.title: App Connector Selection using Access Policies
body: You can now configure an Access Policy to specify the App Connectors that should be used for accessing an application. To learn more, see Configuring Access Policies.

As part of this change, the Policy role was updated and new resource types "Policy to Connector Group Association" and "Policy to Server Group Association" were added. To learn more, see Configuring Administrator Roles and About Audit Logs.
# Session Status Updates

The User Activity log now has a new error code to indicate an App Connector is not configured in a Server Group. (The internal error code is BRK_MT_SETUP_FAIL_CONNECTOR_GROUPS_MISSING.) To learn more, see About ZPA Session Status Codes.
# Resolved Issues
The following issue was resolved:
- A fix was released to address an issue where, under certain circumstances, an error occurred while resetting an Admin account password on the ZPA Admin Portal.

entries.title: Admin Portal Improvements
body: For the Time Range filter on the Application Dashboard and Users Dashboard, you can now set a Custom Range in increments of 15 minute intervals.

entries.title: ZPA Private Service Edge Version 20.93.3
body: This ZPA Private Service Edge version includes an update to address an issue where the ZPA Private Service Edges were not correctly processing updates to policy configurations.

Your ZPA Private Service Edge will be updated based on your software update schedule as configured per ZPA Private Service Edge group. To learn more, see About ZPA Private Service Edge Software Upgrades.

entries.title: Cloud Updates
body: The Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) Cloud now includes an enhancement to the communication methodology between the ZPA Public Service Edge and the Path Selection service in order to improve the performance of information sharing between the two components.

entries.title: Admin Portal Improvements
body: In order to improve user experience, the Diagnostic pages will now display search results up to 500 pages. You can filter results using the available search criteria.

entries.title: Resolved Issues
body: The following issues were resolved:
- A fix was released to address an issue where the ZPA Public Service Edges and ZPA Private Service Edges were not correctly processing updates to policy configurations.

- A fix was released to address an issue where the connection close request from the Zscaler Client Connector was processed by the ZPA Public Service Edge or ZPA Private Service Edge prior to completing the data transfer for that connection.

entries.title: Graphical View of Configuration Objects in the ZPA Admin Portal
body: The Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) Admin Portal now provides a visual layout of the different ZPA configuration objects. You can see this graphical view from the following pages:
- Application Segments
- Segment Groups
- App Connectors
- App Connector Groups
- Server Groups
- Health Dashboard
To view the layout as it relates to a particular object, use the graph icon ().
See image.
The graphical view shows the object and all the other objects it connects to.
See image.

entries.title: ZPA Private Service Edge
body: A ZPA Private Service Edge allows you to host the ZPA Service Edge functionality in your organization’s environment. It is designed to function as single-tenant (per customer) instance, which Zscaler manages. To learn more, see About ZPA Private Service Edges.
Private Service Edge requires Zscaler Client Connector version 2.1.2 at the minimum.
The Service Edge page displays information on each ZPA Private Service Edge you've configured. To learn more, see About ZPA Private Service Edges and Configuring Service Edges.
See image.

Similar to App Connectors, ZPA Private Service Edges are deployed in groups and use provisioning keys. The Service Edge Group page and the Service Edge Provisioning Keys page allows you to view and manage your groups and the keys for your organization's ZPA Private Service Edges. To learn more, see About ZPA Private Service Edge Groups and About ZPA Private Service Edge Provisioning Keys.
See image.
See image.

The Service Edge Status Diagnostics allows for monitoring and tracking all ZPA Public Service Edges and ZPA Private Service Edges. To learn more, see About ZPA Private Service Edge Status Diagnostics.
See image.

In addition, new sections and filters for monitoring and tracking ZPA Public Service Edges and ZPA Private Service Edges were added or updated for Live Logs, User Activity, User Status, App Connector Status, and Application Status. To learn more, see About Live Logs, About User Activity Diagnostics, About User Status Diagnostics, and About App Connector Diagnostics.

entries.title: App Connector Release 20.93.2
body: This App Connector software version includes updates to the software architecture to provide an improved performance when processing application traffic.
Your App Connectors will be updated based on your software update schedule as configured per App Connector group. To learn more, see About App Connector Software Updates.

entries.title: Admin Portal Improvements
body: The following updates were made to the Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) Admin Portal:
- The maximum number of rules for Access policies has increased to 2000 rules. This was raised from 500 policy rules. To learn more, see Ranges & Limitations.
- An update was made to the workflow for editing application segments to provide an improved user experience. To learn more, see Editing Application Segments.
- The Users dashboard now allows you to download the list of Current Connected Users. To learn more, see About the Users Dashboard.

- The ZPA Admin Portal was updated to ensure that users with admin privileges are not unintentionally deleted or have their permissions downgraded. This only impacts system generated user accounts that start with “admin” or “zpaadmin”.
# Resolved Issues
The following issues were resolved:
- A fix was released to address an issue where the Admin UI displayed an error when editing an application segment with browser access applications.
- A fix was released to address an issue where the Admin UI displayed incorrect results when filtering application configuration information with the Contains operator.
- A fix was released to address an issue that sometimes prevented admins from editing policies in the ZPA Admin Portal after returning from the Zscaler Client Connector portal.
- A fix was released to address an issue that prevented the ability to edit policies when an admin was assigned to a custom policy role.
- A fix was released to update the color indication from green to blue for Open or Active transactions on the Diagnostic pages.

entries.title: Cloud Updates
body: The Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) now sets the sameSite attribute to None in the ZPA Browser Access authentication cookies.
# Resolved Issues
The following issue was resolved:

- A fix was released to address an issue where authentication failed for ZPA Browser Access with error code 42018. In this situation, the Browser Access service will now retry single sign-on more than once.

entries.title: Admin Portal Enhancements
body: For a Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) tenant that is associated with Zscaler Client Connector tenants on separate clouds, the ZPA Admin Portal now allows you to select the Zscaler Client Connector tenant and cloud prior to connecting to the Zscaler Client Connector Portal.
Labels and text throughout the ZPA Admin Portal were updated to reflect the Zscaler product name change.
# Resolved Issues
The following issue was resolved:
- A fix was released to change the default Health Reporting setting when configuring an application segment from Continuous to On Access.

entries.title: App Connector Release 20.78.1
body: This App Connector software version includes the following improvement:
- For an App Connector that is explicitly configured to send traffic to a proxy, you can configure the App Connector to bypass the proxy for traffic that needs to be sent to specific destinations.
Your App Connectors will be updated based on your software update schedule as configured per App Connector group. To learn more, see About App Connector Software Updates.

entries.title: Cloud Updates
body: The Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) Cloud now includes an enhancement to the ZPA Policy engine for improved efficiency and scale.

For applications that are still configured to use the already deprecated Application Group policies, transactions will display the following error: "Policy is not configured for access". (The internal error code is BRK_MT_SETUP_FAIL_NO_POLICY_FOUND). To learn more, see About ZPA Session Status Codes.
Application Group policies were deprecated starting January 2018.
To resolve this error, you need to define access policy rules for applications. To learn more, see About Access Policy.

entries.title: Support for OPTIONS Method in Browser Access
body: When enabling browser access for an application, you can now choose whether to allow ZPA to forward an unauthenticated HTTP preflight OPTIONS request from the browser to the application. To learn more, see Configuring Application Segments.
# Admin Portal Improvements

In order to improve the way application segment health is managed in the ZPA Admin Portal, the Health Reporting and Health Check are now consolidated into one setting within the Application Segment workflow. To learn more, see Understanding Health Reporting.
# Resolved Issues
The following issues were resolved:
- A fix was released to address an issue where browser access logs were not always reaching a log receiver.
- A fix was released to address an issue where the application segment search name filter would not display search results if the case did not match.
- A fix was released to address an issue where ZPA did not reorder Access Policy rules correctly when rules were deleted while a reorder of the rules was in progress.
- A fix was released in the ZPA Admin Portal UI to allow trailing spaces in configuration fields.
- A fix was released to update labels in the Connector Dashboard from Mtunnel Count to New Application Tunnels.

entries.title: Admin Portal Enhancements
body: The following update was made to the Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) Admin Portal:
- Applications can now be defined by only a wildcard (e.g., *). To learn more, see Configuring Application Segments.
This configuration method requires approval from Zscaler prior to implementation.

entries.title: App Connector Release 20.51.3
body: This App Connector software version includes the following improvements:
- The amount of available memory for App Connectors is now calculated as the sum of free memory and any cached memory for the system.
- The App Connector logs now show the App Connector uptime as a readable string with the format: "X days Y hours Z seconds".
- The App Connector will log the CPU, memory, and disk utility stats in the App Connector status logs.
- A fix was released to correctly display the number of file descriptors in the App Connector logs.
Your App Connectors will be updated based on your software update schedule as configured per App Connector group. To learn more, see About App Connector Software Updates.

entries.title: Session Status Updates
body: In order to better track what causes an App Connector to not complete a transaction, ZPA now has new error codes for file and port exhaustion. To learn more, see About ZPA Session Status Codes.
# Resolved Issues
- A fix was released to address a performance degradation issue that occurred when the Public Service Edge was processing large volumes of traffic.
- A fix was released to address a performance degradation issue that occurred when the Public Service Edge was processing source IP anchoring traffic.

- A fix was released to address an issue where the server IP and port were not displaying for the error code “Connector: Connection request to server timed out” in the App Connector Diagnostic page in the ZPA Admin Portal.

entries.title: App Connector Release 20.40.7
body: This App Connector software version includes the following improvement:
- A fix was released to address an issue where enabling the Zscaler Client Connector can receive CNAME setting was not processed correctly when configuring an application segment.
Your App Connectors will be updated based on your software update schedule as configured per App Connector group. To learn more, see About App Connector Software Updates.

entries.title: Cloud Updates
body: The following update was made to the Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) Cloud:
- A fix was released to address an issue where enabling Zscaler Client Connector can receive CNAME was not processed correctly when configuring an application segment.

entries.title: Cloud Updates
body: The following updates were made to the Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) Cloud:
- A fix was released to address an issue where users connect to a Private Service Edge further away than a closer Public Service Edge.

entries.title: Source IP Anchoring
body: Source IP Anchoring allows organizations to selectively steer traffic processed by ZIA back to your network. This is done by directing the traffic to the appropriate destination server using the IP address of your choice, which goes through an App Connector. To use Source IP Anchoring, your organization requires both ZIA and ZPA. To learn more, see About Source IP Anchoring.

To enable Source IP Anchoring in ZPA, you need to configure the application segments that require source IP anchoring and set up access policies for ZIA. To learn more, see Configuring Source IP Anchoring.

entries.title: Audit Log in the Log Streaming Service
body: The Log Streaming Service (LSS) now supports streaming of Audit Logs from your organization’s ZPA tenant to your log receiver. To learn more, see About the Log Streaming Service.
# Admin Portal Improvements
The following changes were made to the Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) Admin Portal:
- The search field on list pages was replaced with filters. This provides an improved way to sort through the configuration.
- To improve load time when displaying a large number of users, pagination was added to the Current Connected Users widget on the User Dashboard.
- To improve the experience of Admins in the ZPA Admin Portal, the relationship graph in the Connector section of the Health Dashboard has been deprecated.
# Resolved Issues
The following issues were resolved:
- A fix was released to address an issue where the UI was incorrectly processing the web server certificate during upload.
- A fix was released to address an issue with displaying the access policy filters in Live Logs.
- A fix was released to address a problem where User Status logs were not ingested by some SIEMs when empty fields were not properly defined.

entries.title: App Connector Release 20.28.5
body: This App Connector software version includes the following improvements:
- Additional timestamps were added to User Activity Logs and to messages used for communication between the Service Edge, Central Authority, and App Connector components of the ZPA cloud.
- A fix was released to address an issue related to DNS resolution of applications with multiple IPs.
Your App Connectors will be updated based on your software update schedule as configured per App Connector group. To learn more, see About App Connector Software Updates.

entries.title: Admin Portal Improvements and Cloud Updates
body: The following updates were made to the Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) Admin Portal and ZPA Cloud:
- The number of applications per application segment is now 2000 applications. This was raised from 100 applications per application segment. To learn more, see Ranges & Limitations.

- By default, Zscaler Client Connector (Z App) receives CNAME DNS records from the App Connectors. The Admin Portal now provides an option where the App Connectors will not send CNAME DNS records to Zscaler Client Connector. This is not applicable for Browser Access applications. To learn more, see Configuring Application Segments.

- The ZPA Admin Portal UI will no longer show the application RTT time (i.e., App Connector: App RTT) in the logs. In its place is the time the App Connector takes to process and set up a connection to the application server (i.e., Connection: Setup Time). Connection setup time is connection processing time plus connector to app rtt.
- The Signing Certificate label was changed to Enrollment Certificate in the ZPA Admin Portal for better consistency with certificate’s purpose.

- Your organization can now configure ZPA, so user traffic is processed by a subset of ZPA Public Service Edges that are available in the global ZPA service. Contact Zscaler Support to request access to this feature.

- After the initial authentication from Zscaler Client Connector or App Connectors, the respective control TLS sessions will be established to the the closest available in-country ZPA Public Service Edge.
# Resolved Issues
The following issues were resolved
- A fix was released to address a problem where the Total count on the Diagnostics page would not adjust to accommodate numbers greater than 999 million.
- A fix was released to address audit logs not getting generated while updating the identity provider configuration.
- A fix was released to resolve an issue where the Health dashboard did not display health information consistently.
- A fix was released where the authentication service in ZPA always signed the SAML request to the IdP while ignoring the sign request settings from the IdP.

entries.title: App Connector Release 20.20.5
body: A fix was released for this software version to address an issue where the App Connector disconnected data connections when it was not able to successfully resolve DNS for these existing connections.
Your App Connectors will be updated based on your software update schedule as configured per App Connector Group. To learn more, see About App Connector Software Updates.

entries.title: Cloud Update
body: The following update was made to the Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) Cloud:
- A fix was released to address an issue where the Public Service Edge connection state in the ZPA Central Authority (CA) was incorrect and led to application access issues.

entries.title: Cloud Updates
body: The following update was made to the Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) Cloud:

- A fix was released to address an issue with Browser Access applications where ZPA did not correctly process SAML requests and responses that came out of order. The issue was observed for the Azure AD and Okta identity providers.
- A fix was released where updates to permissions for existing roles may take up to two minutes to take effect in the ZPA Admin Portal.
- A fix was released to address an issue with incorrect username formats that prevented SCIM from processing requests to delete users.

entries.title: Application Segment Updates
body: The Application Segment page of the ZPA Admin Portal is updated to help you gain a better view of your applications. For application segments with more than 3 applications, there is now a link in the table to bring up the Application Segment Details window with all the applications. This is a read only view. From here you can search for applications, ports, certificates, etc. To learn more, see About Applications.
See image.

While editing your application segments, the edit window also provides a search capability and makes sure you do not accidentally enter the same application more than once. Editing now has a multi-tab window similar to configuring an application segment. You can address general application segment details, then manage how applications are defined, and finally review all changes before saving. To learn more, see Editing Application Segments.
See image.
All browser access applications are still marked by the icon, and all other applications are now marked by the icon.

entries.title: App Connector Release 20.20.3
body: This App Connector software version includes the following improvements:

- Enable Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) Public Service Edges (formerly Zscaler Enforcement Nodes or ZENs) to redirect an App Connector's control connection to the geographically closest Public Service Edge. This is based on the load for ZPA Public Service Edges and the App Connector's geolocation.
- This release contains software updates to support the new ZPA Private Service Edge functionality. To learn more, see About ZPA Private Service Edges.
- A fix was released to resolve an issue where the App Connector would crash if the App Connector process was started after creating a tunnel interface.
- A fix was released to address an issue where an App Connector would experience service degradation when it could not identify a Mac address of a tunnel interface.
- A fix was released to reduce the log volume of connection status logs during the normal course of an App Connector’s operation.
- There are new OVA and RPM packages for version 2020.06 available for deploying App Connectors.
- Starting with OVA version 2020.06, rsyslogd is disabled for App Connectors.
- A fix was released to address an App Connector software degradation issue that occurred when the App Connector was processing traffic for applications enabled for double encryption.
Your App Connectors will be updated based on your software update schedule as configured per App Connector Group. To learn more, see About App Connector Software Updates.

entries.title: Cloud Updates
body: The following update was made to the Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) Cloud:
- A fix was released for the ZPA system to issue an error when a SAML response from an identity provider is signed by an expired certificate.

entries.title: Cloud Updates
body: The wait time for the browser access service to get a response from a web server has increased from 20 seconds to 300 seconds. This is to ensure the browser access service can support web servers that have a delay in their response.

entries.title: Cloud Updates
body: The following updates were made to the Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) Cloud:
- A fix was released to resolve an issue with maintaining a user's connection to the same App Connector.

- A fix was released to address an issue where Zscaler Client Connector (Z App) did not receive the correct port ranges for applications configured in ZPA when the port ranges were configured out of order.

- When a username attribute that was learned via SCIM is updated to a new value, ZPA deletes the former username and its associated information from the database. After this, Zscaler Client Connector will terminate the user’s ZPA session and display a Connection Error if the user is connected to ZPA with the former username. The user has to log out of Zscaler Client Connector and re-log in to connect to ZPA.

entries.title: App Connector Dashboard
body: There is now a App Connector dashboard available on the ZPA Admin Portal. This dashboard allows you to monitor the health of your organization's App Connectors and diagnose issues.
See image.
From within the dashboard, you can:
- View graphs and charts for elements of a App Connector or that interact with a App Connector.
- Edit the App Connector.
- Access the App Connector Status diagnostic information for a specific App Connector.
See image.
To learn more, see About the App Connector Dashboard.
# Resolved Issues
The following issues were resolved:

- A fix was released to address a traffic steering issue where less optimal App Connectors were selected for Application Segments that were configured with Health Check set to None. This issue was only observed for App Connectors with software version 20.11.20.

entries.title: App Connector Release 20.11.20
body: This App Connector software version includes the following improvements:

- Resolved an issue where some App Connectors that upgraded from version 19.102.3 to 20.11.13 experienced performance degradation when processing updates from another microservice or when resolving nested DNS CNAME records.

- To reduce the volume of DNS traffic that App Connectors and different ZPA microservices process, ZPA Central Authority (CA) will only send DNS requests to a maximum of two available App Connectors within a App Connector group during the application discovery process.

- App Connectors will no longer send application availability messages to the ZPA CA when Application Segments are configured with Health Reporting set to On Access and Health Check set to Disabled. This change means:
- The ZPA CA will assume the application is reachable through the App Connectors.
- There is a reduction in the volume of application availability messages sent by App Connectors and processed by the ZPA CA.
- The process for selecting a connector for a requested application is faster.
- Additional fields have been added to the App Connector Status logs for visibility and troubleshooting.
- App Connectors will automatically restart if the available disk space is less than 100 MB.
Your App Connectors will be updated based on your software update schedule as configured per App Connector Group. To learn more, see About App Connector Software Updates.

entries.title: User Experience Enhancements
body: The following user experience enhancements were made to the Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) Admin Portal dashboards:

- Numbers in the banner counters that can be rendered with a comma now will be displayed with the comma. For example, Successful Transactions would previously show a number as 234567. Whereas now, it will appear as 234,567.
- The Application Dashboard and the Users Dashboard were updated to change the default time range from 24 hours to 1 hour to improve usability on the ZPA Admin Portal.
- When selecting a custom date range, the End Date is automatically set to the system's current time.
To learn more, see About the Applications Dashboard and About the Users Dashboard.
The following user experience changes were made to the Health dashboard on the Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) Admin Portal:
- When there are more than 200 applications associated with a App Connector, the dashboard will no longer provide a visual representation of those associations when viewing a App Connector.
- The dashboard will no longer show a Servers section.
To learn more, see About the Health Dashboard.
The following changes were made to the Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) Admin Portal:

- During single sign-on (SSO) into the ZPA Admin Portal, a customer's identity provider (IdP) must cryptographically sign the SAML assertion in the response or sign the entire SAML response. ZPA will prevent SSO into the ZPA Admin Portal if either of these two requirements are not met. To learn more, see About IdP Configuration.
# Resolved Issues
The following issues were resolved:
- A fix was released to resolve the count mismatch that was occurring between the counts displayed on the Applications and Users dashboards and the count when those data sets were downloaded.
- A fix was released to resolve an issue where application segments, server groups, and access policies were not created or available to update due to a “payload.size.exceeded” error.
- A fix was released to address a problem where some users were logged out of the ZPA Admin Portal after logging in.

- A fix was released to improve search functionality and search response time on the Diagnostic pages. There is now a three character minimum requirement for suggestions to appear in the search drop-down.

- A fix was released to limit the number of suggested entries to 30 in the drop-down list for filters on the Diagnostics page. Administrators will need to specify more granular entries for search values to narrow suggestions in the drop-down list.

entries.title: App Connector Release 20.11.13
body: This App Connector software version resolves the following issue:
- An improvement was made to how App Connectors process a large number of DNS queries.
Your App Connectors will be updated based on your software update schedule as configured per App Connector Group. To learn more, see About App Connector Software Updates.

entries.title: App Connector Release 19.102.3
body: This App Connector software version includes an enhancement to reduce the duration for which App Connectors consume a UDP socket, so that UDP sockets are used more efficiently. If the App Connector is requesting applications on UDP ports 88, 123, 161, or 389, the App Connector will release the UDP socket after 2 seconds from the instance it started consuming the socket. For access on all other UDP ports, the App Connector will continue to hold onto UDP socket for 60 seconds.
Your App Connectors will be updated based on your software update schedule as configured per App Connector group. To learn more, see About App Connector Software Updates.

entries.title: Admin Portal UI Warnings for Incomplete Configuration
body: You can now see warnings when viewing or editing a server, server group, segment group, or application segment that is missing important configuration information.
See image.
To learn more, see About Servers, About Server Groups, About Segment Groups, and About Applications.

entries.title: System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM)
body: You can now configure SCIM for user and group management. It allows for faster deprovisioning of users from ZPA when you delete them in your user directory. To learn more, see About SCIM.
The Edit IdP Configuration window allows you to enable SCIM syncing between ZPA and an IdP.
See image.
To learn more, see Enabling SCIM for Identity Management.
When you enable SCIM syncing and configure an IdP for SCIM, the SCIM Attributes page allows you to view all SCIM attributes coming from the IdP.
See image.
To learn more, see About SCIM.
Microsoft Azure Active Directory (AD) supports SCIM for ZPA. To learn more, see About SCIM and SCIM Configuration Guide for Microsoft Azure AD.

entries.title: Client Forwarding Policy
body: You can now create policy rules that define when application requests are forwarded to ZPA from the Zscaler Client Connector (Z App). When configuring a client forwarding policy rule, you can apply one of the following actions:

- Bypass ZPA - If selected, Zscaler Client Connector (Z App) will not send application requests to ZPA. This setting is the equivalent of selecting Always for the Bypass setting within an application segment.

- Only Forward Allowed Applications - If you only want Zscaler Client Connector to forward user requests for applications that they are allowed to access, select this action. The list of applications that the user has access to is defined by the access policy. To learn more, see About Access Policy. This setting also controls the list of applications that Zscaler Client Connector processes when evaluating application requests for ZPA. Zscaler Client Connector will forward requests for applications that the user is not allowed to access on their local network. So, these requests will not be logged in Zscaler Client Connector or ZPA.

- Forward to ZPA - If selected, Zscaler Client Connector will forward application requests to ZPA. This includes requests to applications that the user is not authorized to access. This is selected by default.
See image.
To learn more, see About Client Forwarding Policy and Configuring Client Forwarding Policies.
In addition, the Add Application Segment window now displays the following options for the Bypass setting:

- Use Client Forwarding Policy (formerly Never): The decision to forward a user’s application request to ZPA is defined by the client forwarding policy. If none of the policy rules apply, then access to the application is implicitly set to Forward to ZPA. This is also the case if you do not define any client forwarding policy rules at all within the ZPA Admin Portal. This option is selected by default.

- Always: Users can always bypass ZPA when accessing an application. Only choose this option if you've enabled dynamic application discovery and you want users to access the defined application without ZPA.

- On Corporate Network: Users can bypass ZPA when accessing an application from a trusted network. ZPA checks if the user is on a trusted network defined in the Zscaler Client Connector forwarding profile.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring Application Segments and Configuring Bypass Settings.
# Updates to Diagnostics and Log Streaming Service

In addition to the above changes, the User Activity, User Status, and App Connector Status Log Types under Diagnostics were all updated to support Client Forwarding Policy field data, and provide user metadata information in particular. The User Status and User Activity log fields used to define Log Stream Content for the Log Streaming Service (LSS) were also updated.
# Resolved Issues

The SUCCESSFUL filter that appears at the top of the Diagnostics > User Activity page now displays the correct abbreviated text when the value is over 100 million (i.e., 100M+ is displayed instead of the complete number).

entries.title: User Experience Improvements to Dashboard
body: The following enhancements were made to the dashboards within the ZPA Admin Portal in order to improve usability:
- On the Applications dashboard, the Discovered Applications widget was renamed to Applications Discovered in Past 14 Days.

- You can now download application and user information to a file (.csv) for the following widgets on the Applications and Users dashboards: Applications Accessed, Applications Discovered in Past 14 Days, and Recent Users.
See image.
- The Applications Accessed and Applications Discovered in Past 14 Days widgets now display the application's port number.
See image.
To learn more, see About the Applications Dashboard and About the Users Dashboard.

entries.title: User Portals for End-Users & Partners
body: You can now create user portals for your end-users that contain direct links to private and public applications that they have access to.
See image.
A new User Portal section within the ZPA Admin Portal' main navigation menu is available, where you can:
- Configure your user portals. To learn more, see About User Portals.
- Configure the links that appear within your user portals. To learn more, see About Portal Links.

- Configure the download links for the Zscaler Client Connector, so end-users can download and install Zscaler Client Connector directly from a user portal. To learn more, see About Zscaler Client Connector Download Links.
- Configure an Acceptable Use Policy (AUP) for your user portals. To learn more, see About User Portal Acceptable Use Policy.
See image.
To learn more about how end-users can access and navigate your portals, see Accessing a User Portal.
When an end-user's session expires, the user portal might become unresponsive. If this occurs, they will need to reauthenticate into the portal in order to continue accessing applications.
In addition, the following session status error codes were added and updated:
- ZPA BA: TLS Wrong Version Number (EXPTR_MT_TLS_SETUP_FAIL_VERSION_MISMATCH)
- ZPA BA: CA Not Trusted (EXPTR_MT_TLS_SETUP_FAIL_NOT_TRUSTED_CA)
- ZPA BA: Certificate Chaining Issue (EXPTR_MT_TLS_SETUP_FAIL_CERT_CHAIN_ISSUE)
- ZPA BA: TLS setup failed (EXPTR_MT_TLS_SETUP_FAIL_PEER)
To learn more, see About ZPA Session Status Codes.

entries.title: DNS Search Domain Enhancements
body: Within the DNS Search Domains window, you can now specify if you want the Zscaler Client Connector (Z App) to resolve invalid domains as NXDOMAINs (non-existent domains).
This functionality is only available to users running Zscaler Client Connector 1.5.1 or later.
In addition, you can now remove domains from the list by mousing over the field and clicking the Remove icon:
See image.
To learn more, see Adding DNS Search Domains.
# ZPA Admin Portal Enhancements
The following enhancements where made to the ZPA Admin Portal in this release:
- The ability to remove items (i.e., domains, applications, port ranges, etc.) within a configuration using the Remove icon. You can also remove the first entry in the list.
See image.

- Zscaler recommends excluding DNS traffic (port 53) from TCP and UDP port ranges within an application segment. So, the Add/Edit Application Segment window will display a warning message whenever you attempt to include port 53 within a TCP/UDP port range.
- The Expand/Collapse All option was moved to the top of each page.
See image.

- ZPA now supports a maximum SAML assertion size of 1MB when authenticating users via Browser Access or Zscaler Client Connector (Z App). If a user’s SAML assertion size is greater then 60KB, then Zscaler Client Connector 2.0.1 is required on PCs. For mobile devices, the maximum SAML assertion size that Zscaler Client Connector supports will continue to be 60KB.

entries.title: ZPA Admin Portal User Experience Enhancements
body: The following enhancements were made to the ZPA Admin Portal in order to improve usability:
- Using the new Admin Portal Session Timeout field on the Administration > Settings page, you can specify how long ZPA admins can be inactive on the Admin Portal before they are logged out.
See image.
To learn more see, Configuring Authentication Settings. Also, when adding or editing ZPA admin roles, the Authentication access control section was updated to include Settings.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring Administrator Roles.
- The Remote Assistance field was moved from the Settings page to the Help () menu.
- To learn more, see About Remote Assistance.
- You can now search by application segment name, domain name, or IP address on the Administration > Application Segments page. To learn more, see About Applications.
- If you have the ZPA Read Only Administrator role, you will now be able to view audit logs. To learn more, see About Audit Logs.

entries.title: Multiple Identity Provider Support for Single Sign-On
body: You can now add and configure multiple identity providers (IdPs) in order to support single sign-on (SSO) for users and admins. This allows you to add as many IdPs for user and admin SSO as your organization requires, while enabling you to configure policies for the user traffic coming into ZPA from those various IdPs.
The Add IdP Configuration window displays a workflow that guides you through the configuration process:
See image.
The IdP Configuration page also displays new information on each IdP you've configured:
See image.

If you have any existing IdP configurations, the IdP will continue to work as desired. However, for the Single Sign-On field, the Both setting is no longer an option for new IdP configurations as you can now configure as many IdPs as needed for both admin and user SSO.
To learn more, see About IdP Configuration and Configuring an IdP for Single Sign-On.
